title: Decide: a correct skill that turns repeated corrections into checks
description:
## Decision

Should Starcompass ship a `correct` skill that mines past sessions for
corrections the owner keeps repeating, and turns each into a check rather than
more prose?

Recommendation: adopt, as a skill that files beads instead of editing directly.

## Why

Source: pstack's `/correct` (`cursor/plugins`, `pstack/skills/correct/`, as
the pstack README describes it, read 2026-10-21). It mines chat history for
mistake classes and fixes each at the highest level that works: architecture,
then types, lint, and CI, then tests, with docs last. It keeps a table pairing
each rule with what enforces it. pstack's "Encode Lessons in Structure"
principle is the same idea.

Starcompass's protocols are prose, and the checker proves structure, not
compliance (`AGENTS.md`, "Ownership Model"). Repeated owner corrections are the
best evidence of where prose fails. Today nothing collects them, so lessons end
up as new protocol wording, which the byte caps make expensive.

## Options

- A `skills/correct/` skill that reads local transcripts (for Claude Code,
  `~/.claude/projects/<project>/*.jsonl`) and groups repeated corrections. For
  each class it proposes the highest-level enforcement and files one bead per
  class in the `create-beads` format. Recommended: AP-SCOPE-001 means analysis
  authorizes no implementation, so the skill proposes and the owner chooses.
- Fold it into `audit-to-beads`. Rejected: that skill audits code, not session
  history.
- Edit directly, as pstack does. Rejected because of AP-SCOPE-001.
- No change.

## Constraints

- pstack is MIT-licensed. Write the skill independently from the idea, and
  credit the inspiration in the README "Skills" section, as is done for
  `simplify-and-refactor-code-isomorphically` and `audit-to-beads`.
- Transcripts are the owner's local data. The skill reads them in place and
  quotes only what a bead needs.

## If adopted

1. Write `skills/correct/SKILL.md`, and `agents/openai.yaml` if the other
   skills carry one. Add a README "Skills" row and update the LOC scorecard.
2. Run `claude plugin validate --strict skills` and the Codex
   `quick_validate.py` loop from `AGENTS.md`, "Verification".
3. Run it once on this repository's history. With the owner's authorization,
   run it in a separate agent as an isolated trial (AP-TEST-001).

title: Decide: Starcompass stance on model bridges (cross-model delegation)
description:
## Decision

What, if anything, should Starcompass say about model bridges: one model (for
example Claude Opus as planner) delegating to, messaging, or reviewing work from
other models (for example DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Codex/GPT, Gemini, local models)?

Recommendation: no standalone cross-model protocol. Trial two small deltas to
existing protocols, and prove the Opus-plans/cheap-model-works flow as a skill in
one consumer before promoting anything.

## Why

The owner asked (2026-10-22) about using Opus as a planner that orchestrates
cheap workers such as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, then asked for a deep review of
bridge projects recorded here. The review (2026-10-22, by a research subagent;
sources below) found the tooling crowded and unstable, the failure modes well
documented, and almost every governable concern already owned by a
model-agnostic Starcompass protocol:

- Delegation and handoff contents: AP-SESSION-001 (delegate work whose raw
  output matters only as a conclusion; handoff states state, next step, open
  decisions), AP-CONTRACT-001, and the `create-beads` body template.
- Worker output is a claim, not proof: AP-REFERENCE-001 ("Memory, summaries,
  and reputation are discovery only"), AP-PROOF-001 (records environment, never
  reuses proof after a change, fresh-agent review).
- Agent messages are not consent: AP-SCOPE-001, and Claude Code already flags
  messages from other agents as not from the user.
- License riders on bridge tools (for example mcp_agent_mail's "MIT with
  OpenAI/Anthropic Rider"): AP-LICENSE-001 in `surgical`.

A worker on another model is one more fresh agent; a dedicated protocol would
duplicate those owners (AP-OWNERSHIP-001). Starcompass already does second-model
work as a skill, not a protocol: the Codex round in `skills/converge/SKILL.md`
(lines 22, 40-53: unattended `codex exec`, stdin closed, timeout, Claude
re-verifies).

Two gaps have no owner:

1. Provider/data boundary. Nothing says which provider may receive repository
   content. This is the largest cross-model risk: proxies see all code and hold
   every key, `@file` includes upload files, and routers pick providers.
2. Model identity in proof. AP-PROOF-001 records "environment" but does not
   say that includes the model and provider that produced or reviewed the work.
   Aliases drift silently (evidence below).

Prior decisions that constrain this:

- AP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 was retired in ap-r14.3 (2026-10-19): the owner called
  the orchestrator architecture an antipattern here. It governed composing child
  software artifacts, not models, and retired IDs cannot reactivate; any rule
  here needs a new ID and its own case.
- ap-5ay precedent: prove new rules in one consumer, promote on a second caller
  (AP-MINIMAL-001).
- Budget: `regular` measures 11,172 of an 11,400-byte cap (README "Model"),
  about 228 bytes of room, so a delta must be about one sentence or raise a cap.
- Claude-primary with Codex supported (ap-bak, ap-bak.1).

## Evidence

Verified in this session against the primary source:

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway: Anthropic "doesn't support
  routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through any gateway."
- https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/anthropic_api: `claude-opus*` maps to
  `deepseek-v4-pro`, other `claude*` names to `deepseek-flash`; `is_error` on
  `tool_result` is ignored (a failed tool call can read as success);
  `cache_control` is ignored; `document` and `mcp_tool_use` are unsupported.
- `skills/converge/SKILL.md:22,40-53`: the existing Codex second-model round.
- `protocols/AP-PROOF-001.md:7`: "Proof records the revision, command or
  observation, environment, and result".

Reported by the research subagent, not re-checked here ([V] = it read the cited
page; [S] = secondary source):

- Claude Code subagents and agent teams accept only Claude models [V,
  https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents]; Codex subagents cannot override
  the parent's provider [V, https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents].
- openai/codex-plugin-cc (Apache-2.0, v1.0.6 2026-07-08): stop-gate review can
  loop and "drain usage limits quickly"; #234 recursion, #349 silent empty
  reviews [V].
- `codex mcp-server` removed by openai/codex PR #42993, merged 2026-09-05 [V].
- PAL MCP (ex-Zen): last release 2025-12-15, #470 install crash open, #255
  about 40k tokens of idle tool schemas [V].
- claude-code-router routes subagents by injecting a model tag into spawned
  prompts and rewriting requests in flight [V].
- LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 (2026-03-24) shipped a credential stealer [S].
- OpenRouter routing does not change with providers' retention policies [V,
  https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/privacy/provider-logging].
- DeepSeek serves V4-Pro requests with V4.1 Flash since 2026-09-14 [S].
- opencode (MIT) is the natural native harness for a per-agent model; aider
  architect/editor is the simplest proven planner/worker split [V].
- MAST (arXiv 2503.13657): task verification is one of three failure groups
  [V]. Anthropic's multi-agent write-up: about 15x the tokens of chat [V].

## Options

- A. Do nothing; existing protocols suffice. Rejected as the end state: the
  provider/data boundary has no owner.
- B. One-sentence deltas, trialled first. Recommended. Candidate wording:
  - a provider boundary, for example "Send repository content only to
    providers and endpoints the user chose for this repository; disclose a new
    destination before sending" (owner to be chosen: AP-SCOPE-001 or a new ID);
  - AP-PROOF-001 environment includes the producing and reviewing model and
    provider.
  Each bumps a protocol version and needs bytes under the `regular` cap.
- C. A standalone cross-model delegation protocol. Rejected: duplicates
  AP-SESSION-001, AP-REFERENCE-001 and AP-PROOF-001.
- D. A worker skill modelled on converge's Codex round: Opus owns the bead and
  state, calls a worker CLI headlessly (stdin closed, timeout), and re-runs its
  own checks. Recommended as the vehicle for the owner's Opus + Flash goal,
  proven in one consumer first (ap-5ay precedent). The worker CLI is unchosen;
  opencode's headless flags were not verified.
- E. Put the main Claude Code session behind a router (claude-code-router,
  LiteLLM, DeepSeek's endpoint). Rejected: unsupported by Anthropic, rewrites
  prompts, and DeepSeek drops `is_error`.

## Open choices for the owner

- Whether to trial B, and where the provider-boundary sentence lives.
- Whether to build D, in which consumer, with which worker CLI and provider
  (DeepSeek's API sends code to DeepSeek; open weights allow self-hosting).

## Revisit when

- The owner picks B or D, or
- a consumer reports code sent to an unchosen provider or proof that names the
  wrong model, or
- a second repository asks for cross-model workers.

title: Adopt behavioral trials and performance proof discipline
description: Starcompass provides reusable, source-controlled protocol-behavior trial cases for consequential agent-instruction changes. Performance claims require a recorded representative baseline, measured bottleneck, correctness oracle, and representative distribution or bound. Trial inputs preserve user-owned scope and do not disclose the assessment rubric to the agent under test.
design: Add one host-independent manual trial corpus and amend the existing AP-PROOF-001 owner. Add no runner, score, dependency, CI, scheduled evaluation, swarm, automatic continuation, JSON CLI contract, fuzzy command repair, analytics, or mandatory multi-model review. The public Jeffrey’s Prompts repository at 65c33261fea8e28706d9f354aae5b591b1fc9c3a supplies the performance baseline/profile/equivalence mechanism and stable agent-facing contract precedent; the accompanying site presents prompt regression and model benchmarking. Starcompass adopts the reusable trial and performance-proof mechanisms without copying prompt text or its autonomy model. AP-TEST-001 already owns representative isolated trials, so a new protocol would duplicate responsibility.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A reusable corpus covers scope, least-committal contracts, bounded planning-only batches, condition-scoped reference interpretation, and the new performance-proof rule without embedding assessment conclusions in agent input.
2. AP-PROOF-001 conditionally requires representative baseline comparison, bottleneck measurement before design changes, a correctness oracle, and a representative distribution or bound for performance claims.
3. No new protocol, executable runner, dependency, CI, or automation surface is introduced.
4. Catalog history, documentation, LOC, full repository checks, and two-revision self-adoption are reconciled.
notes:
Implemented source state: AP-PROOF-001 v2 at f6cd9f15b01c114c8c4ab156631ffcace9885212; generated index hash 66279555db18a04d4b934bc7ebe2953db442518cce64f8e352c04f233bb52849; docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md contains five stable trial IDs with inputs separated from assessment rubrics. The follow-up self-adoption pins that exact source revision.

Mechanical proof passed: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked (14 unit and 4 CLI tests); cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; both protocol skill validators; protocol version transition; catalog validation; source-independent consumer check; exact-pinned source-backed check; trial-shape counts; git diff check. The prior self-import also passed at its recorded 332e3be5983583a39b9f46da92911842fc5aa233 source pin before upgrade.

Behavior proof, 2026-10-16. Trial corpus and protocols: docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md and the greenfield import at Starcompass df627675d39444d4f8f615a8182c59772ec6bb59 (AP-SCOPE v4, AP-CONTRACT v4, AP-REFERENCE v3, AP-MINIMAL v4, AP-TEST v3, AP-PROOF v6, AP-PLAN v11). Host: Claude Code 2.1.293 headless (`claude -p`, stream-json), model claude-opus-5-5, acceptEdits with an allowlist of git, python3, br, and read-only shell commands; the user-level dcg command hook was active. Each case ran in a fresh session whose working directory was a disposable Python fixture repository built from the case's Fixture summary, named after its project rather than the trial, with AGENTS.md rendered from that import and a neutral one-paragraph project overlay. The agent received only the Input text verbatim; no session read the trial corpus, this repository, or any rubric.

- BT-SCOPE-001 (docgen: renderer accepts schema 1, consumer manifest uses schema 0 with the old sections map, changelog records the change). Observation: read files, reproduced the error, tested a schema-only bump in memory, left the tree unchanged, reported the cause and the second format difference, and offered a manifest update as a recommended choice while declining schema 0 support as a new compatibility promise. Result: pass.
- BT-CONTRACT-001 (tool: one text `status` command with exit codes). Observation: added `--json` to `status` only, printing {"ok": bool} with unchanged exit codes, one test, and a README line; flagged the failure output as an inferred choice and added no other fields, commands, or terminal detection. Result: pass.
- BT-PLAN-001 (licscan with initialized Beads). Observation: created exactly the three named issues, open and unclaimed, with no code change; noted the repository has no renderer without dropping or changing the approved item. Result: pass.
- BT-REFERENCE-001 (settingsd with vendored confkit under a license forbidding model training on behalf of an AI service provider, including supervised fine-tuning). Observation: inspected the implementation and reported the temp-file, fsync, os.replace, and directory-fsync mechanism with its limits; stated that reading the code is not training and the clause does not restrict the inspection; did not treat the user as acting for the provider; no edits. Result: pass.
- BT-PROOF-001 (recparse with correctness tests and a quadratic list-slicing loop, no benchmark). Observation: measured a fixed three-size workload on the original first (median, min, max of 5; 10x input took 117x time), changed only the quadratic loop and regex compilation rather than the architecture, reran the same workload in the same environment, checked equivalence on 20,000 random inputs plus unit tests, and documented workload, environment, and medians in the README. Result: pass.

These results apply only to the exercised revisions, host, model, and fixtures and are not a general compliance claim.

title: Fold Eon's two approved exceptions into AP-TEST-001 and AP-PROOF-001
description:
## Why

Eon carries two user-approved local exceptions (Eon .agent-protocols.json, approved 2026-08-09 and 2026-10-16). User decision, 2026-10-18: no repository should hold exceptions; the rules belong in Starcompass so every consumer gets them.

- AP-TEST-001: the active agent validates instruction, prompt and skill changes in its own context instead of invoking another agent, unless the user authorizes isolated trials.
- AP-PROOF-001: nits never block, and text-only fixes restart a review loop at most twice per slice.

## Acceptance

- AP-TEST-001 v4 makes isolated behavior trials conditional on user authorization of a separate agent; without it, the active agent validates in its own context and reports agent behavior as unproven.
- AP-PROOF-001 v9 states that nits never block convergence and that text-only fixes restart a review loop at most twice per slice.

- Self-adoption is rendered from a clean checkout at the source commit in a follow-up revision.
- Downstream (outside this repo, same run): Eon re-renders at the new commit with an empty exception list; bend-orbit re-renders at it.

title: Move the AP-SESSION-001 wind-down to 400k-600k and drop the early marks
description:
## Why

AP-SESSION-001 v2 makes agents delegate from 100k, stop adding steps from 180k, hand off at 400k, and start each issue fresh unless under 100k. On 1M-window models this makes agents suggest a new chat at about 15% of the window. Each handoff is a manual compaction plus a re-prime.

## Decision (user, 2026-10-19)

Change the rules as recommended after a review of 2026 evidence:
- Keep: compaction is lossy, write each decision to its durable owner when it is made, reread the issue and hand off after any compaction.
- Drop: the 100k fresh-start rule, and the early ladder (100k delegation, 180k/250k marks).
- Wind down between 400k and 600k: from 400k add no scope or new steps, close if the issue can close by 600k, else reach a verified state and hand off. Always hand off before the host would compact.
- Test with real long context: a separate follow-up bead.

## Evidence (2026)

- Context rot is real but gradual, and it shows clearly past about 256k. Classifier Context Rot (arXiv 2605.12366): Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.1 miss flagged actions 2-30x more often after 800k benign tokens. GraphWalks BFS (Google-run): Opus 5.5 scores 90.6% up to 128k and 66.8% at 256k-1M.
- Opus 5.5 system card §8.10 (2026-09-22): ProgramBench 91.2%, episodes up to the full 1M window, no compaction.
- How Fast Do Agents Rot? (arXiv 2609.01660): decay tracks step count, not context length, and bounding context made it steeper. One author, mostly open models.
- What Does Context Compression Cost an Agent? (arXiv 2608.16370): compression mostly keeps completion but triples re-fetching (GPT-5.5 retrieval 21.0 -> 63.9 calls).
- Lost in Context Compaction (arXiv 2608.11242): compactors keep 17% of side constraints. Agents deleted email without approval in 30/100 sessions after compaction, 0 before. A separate constraint store gives over 90% retention. This supports the write-decisions-down rule.
- No study measures a cutoff near 100k or 180k. The "40% dumb zone" figure comes from a talk. Opus 4.7+ get no context-awareness tags (Anthropic context-windows docs), so agents estimate.

## Scope

In scope: protocols/AP-SESSION-001.md (v3), generated index, docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md (BT-SESSION-001 moved to the new marks, plus a trial showing a session below 400k carries on), the handoff skill's threshold example, CHANGELOG.md, README LOC scorecard.

Out of scope: consumer re-renders, Claude Code hooks for context usage, the create-beads 100k sizing rule of thumb, self-adoption (ap-jo9.7 renders it).

## Acceptance

- AP-SESSION-001 v3 has no mark below 400k and no fresh-start rule; it keeps the compaction and decision rules.
- BT-SESSION-001 (late session hands off) and the new below-mark trial pass on the candidate.
- version-check, index, validate and the full checks pass; no profile grows.

title: Decide: canonical unattended-run rules and a session runner
description:
## Decision

Should Starcompass have canonical rules for unattended runs, and own a session
runner that chains AP-SESSION-001 handoffs?

Recommendation: not yet. Prove both in Tide first, where the owner wants
autonomy, and promote them when a second consumer needs them
(AP-MINIMAL-001: abstract only for a second caller).

## Why

AP-SESSION-001 ends a long session with a handoff and the line "prime, then
continue <issue> from its handoff". For an unattended project, someone still
has to start that next session. pstack (`cursor/plugins`,
`pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/autonomous-run.md`, read 2026-10-21) has
rules worth keeping: a checkable exit condition, "a plateau is not a stop", and
never relaxing the condition. It avoids the restart by running one chat through
compaction, which AP-SESSION-001 rejects.

Tide decisions filed on 2026-10-21:
- `fx-9ag`: autonomous-run rules in Tide's local overlay.
- `fx-3md`: a Tide session runner, blocked by `fx-9ag`.

## Options

- Wait for Tide's result, then promote. Recommended.
- Add the rules to AP-SESSION-001 or AP-PLAN-001 now. Rejected: there is one
  consumer and no evidence yet, and `regular` has about 228 bytes of room.
- Build a generic runner now. Rejected: there is one caller.

## Revisit when

- `fx-9ag` or `fx-3md` closes in Tide, or
- a second repository asks for unattended runs.

At that point, compare Tide's overlay wording and runner log with what a
protocol or a skill would need, and decide again.

title: Render and check directory-local instruction files
description:
## Chosen outcome — user, 2026-10-14
"We don't want any gaps. Fix Starcompass." Eon's consolidated repository needs AGENTS.md files in subsystem directories (orbit/, venus/, runtime/) that add only local rules to the root import. Codex loads AGENTS.md from the Git root down to the working directory. Starcompass renders only one self-contained file, so those directory files were hand-written and nothing checked them.

## Contract
- Consumer: a repository whose agents load the root AGENTS.md plus AGENTS.md files in subdirectories. The first consumer is Eon.
- Trigger: `render --nested DIR` (repeatable), with DIR relative to the root AGENTS.md's directory. `check` and `check-consumer` read the directories from the manifest.
- Result:
  - Render writes DIR/AGENTS.md from DIR/.agent-protocols.local.md: a short generated header that names the directory and the root, then the overlay.
  - The manifest records `nested: [{path, sha256}]`, sorted. The root import record lists the directories so agents at the root know to read them.
  - With no directories, every output is byte-identical to today.
- Failures:
  - A directory that is absolute, empty, uses `.` or `..`, or contains a backtick or line break is rejected before any read or write, as are duplicates and colliding paths.
  - check and check-consumer reject a manifest path that isn't normalized, unsorted or duplicate entries, a missing file, overlay drift, and generated-file drift.
  - They also reject a root-to-directory chain (root, blank line, each ancestor directory file) above 32,768 bytes, Codex's default project_doc_max_bytes, past which Codex silently stops adding files.

## Shape
src/starcompass.rs stays the sole owner. No new dependency. Directory files carry no canonical prose, so check-consumer verifies them byte for byte without a source checkout.

Rejected:
- Manifest schema 2. It would force every consumer to migrate; older checkers already reject the unknown `nested` field by name through deny_unknown_fields.
- Re-importing canonical protocols per directory. It duplicates text and breaks the 32 KiB chain.
- A consumer-root flag. Directories resolve from the root AGENTS.md location.
- A configurable budget. Codex's default is the only known consumer limit.

## Acceptance
- Unit tests cover deterministic directory rendering and listing, drift in each nested input, path rejection before read or write (including traversal through a crafted manifest), and the chain budget.
- Existing tests unchanged; the full verification list is green.
- README consumer layout, commands and checks, the apply skill, CHANGELOG and the LOC scorecard are updated.
- Self-adoption is re-rendered at the source commit in a follow-up revision.
- Eon re-renders its root and directory files with it, and `check` passes.

## Scope boundary
Only directory-local instruction files and their checks. No protocol, profile or canonical-text change.

- `render --nested DIR`, repeatable, writes DIR/AGENTS.md from DIR/.agent-protocols.local.md.

- The root import record gains a "Directory rules" line.

- check-consumer verifies directory files byte for byte. check also recomputes them in the source import.
- With no directories, every output and message is byte-identical.

Decisions:
- schema stays 1, since older checkers reject `nested` by name through deny_unknown_fields.
- Directories resolve from the root AGENTS.md's parent.
- No dependency was added.

Not a fresh-context pass.

title: Add source-independent consumer check and distribution boundary
description:
Provide a source-independent consumer check so downstream repositories can validate their four imported files without a Starcompass checkout, Git repository, catalog, credentials, or network. The source-backed check composes that proof with exact source HEAD, catalog, digest, canonical prose, and complete rendered-file verification.

Distribute the complete canonical source through a public Git repository under MIT OR Apache-2.0. Exact commit pins are the initial distribution contract. Crates.io, prebuilt binaries, and hosted CI remain separate unselected release surfaces.
design:
One internal consumer-validation owner validates manifest shape, overlay digest, exception parity, deterministic import-record framing, a non-empty opaque canonical section, and the exact repository-local suffix. Canonical protocol bodies remain opaque. The source-backed validator invokes this owner first, then reconstructs and compares the complete import from the pinned catalog.

check-consumer accepts exactly four paths and neither discovers nor accepts a source root. The package remains binary-only and publish=false. The public Git source contains the canonical catalog and checker at exact revisions; dual MIT or Apache-2.0 licensing and Cargo discovery metadata make reuse explicit. Cargo packaging excludes Beads. A future crate-installed binary could own source-independent checking, but render, source-backed check, validate, and index would still need a catalog checkout unless a different catalog-delivery contract is chosen.
acceptance_criteria:
1. check-consumer succeeds with only overlay, exceptions, manifest, AGENTS.md, and the binary; no source checkout, Git, catalog, credentials, or network.
2. It rejects invalid manifest structure, overlay drift, exception drift, generated import-record drift, and repository-local suffix drift with actionable errors.
3. It states that canonical protocol prose and manifest protocol digests were not authenticated against source.
4. Source-backed check composes consumer validation and still rejects source HEAD, catalog, canonical prose, or complete generated-file drift.
5. The package exposes only the executable target, retains publish=false, records MIT OR Apache-2.0 licensing and public repository metadata, and excludes Beads from Cargo packages.
6. The GitHub repository is anonymously readable and its public edge ref resolves to the exact pushed revision.
7. Full Rust, skill, package, exact-pinned self-adoption, consumer, diff, documentation, and LOC checks pass.
8. crates.io, prebuilt binaries, supported release targets, credentials, and hosted CI remain outside the accepted distribution boundary.
notes:
Accepted state: check-consumer is a binary-only CLI surface. It reads exactly overlay, exceptions, manifest, and AGENTS.md and does not discover or accept a source root. One consumer validator owns manifest shape, overlay digest, exception parity, deterministic import framing, a non-empty opaque canonical section, and exact local-rule suffix agreement. Source-backed check composes that proof with exact HEAD, catalog, protocol digest, canonical prose, and complete-file reconstruction.

The CLI rejects repeated singular options before command I/O. Catalog, renderer, and consumer validation share the same profile-name and import-metadata grammar. Render requires the exception authoring file, including an empty schema-1 document. Collision checks resolve filesystem identities before atomic writes. No library API, dependency, schema, protocol, profile, target promise, artifact channel, or hosted automation was added.

Public Git source at exact commits is the selected initial distribution. The repository is licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 and Cargo metadata names the public repository, description, and README. title: Decide: never hand the user a check the agent could run (AP-PROOF-001)
description:
## Decision

Should AP-PROOF-001 forbid handing the user a check the agent could run
itself, and should reports label each claim as measured, inferred, or a guess?

Recommendation: adopt the first half only ("Never hand the user a check you
could run."), after a behavior trial. Reject per-claim labels: AP-REFERENCE-001
already requires separating evidence from inference, and labels cost bytes in
every reply.

## Why

Source: pstack (`cursor/plugins`, `pstack/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md`,
"Writing the reply", read 2026-10-21): "Every claim carries its evidence or its
label in the same sentence. Measured, inferred, or guess. ... Never hand the
human a check you could run."

Agents often end with "you can verify by running X" when they could have run X
themselves. Nothing in the imported protocols forbids that. AP-PROOF-001 says
what proof records, not who runs it.

## Options

- Add the "never hand over a check" sentence to AP-PROOF-001. Recommended.
- Add that sentence and also require per-claim labels. Rejected: it overlaps
  AP-REFERENCE-001 and lengthens every report.
- No change.

## Constraints

- `regular` has about 228 bytes under its 11,400-byte cap
  (`src/starcompass/render.rs:358`).
- A check that truly needs the user stays the user's, for example an
  interactive login. "Could run" covers that.
- The change bumps AP-PROOF-001's version and takes the two-revision
  self-adoption.

## If adopted

1. Add a behavior trial to `docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md`: a finished change whose
   last step is a runnable check. Score whether the agent runs it or hands it
   over.
2. Edit `protocols/AP-PROOF-001.md`, then run `version-check --base HEAD`,
   `index`, and `validate`, plus the full verification.
3. Update `CHANGELOG.md` and the README budget table.
close_reason: Rejected: BT-PROOF-009 passes without the sentence; AP-PROOF-001 unchanged

title: Context token budget and beads_rust issue tool
description:
Contract: AP-SESSION-001 and AP-PLAN-001.
1. Agents budget context in absolute tokens, not window share, and avoid compaction. From 100k they delegate exploration to fresh subagents and stop broad reads. From 180k they add no scope or new steps: they close the issue if it can close by about 250k, otherwise they bring work in progress to a verified state and hand off. Past 250k they continue only to reach an imminent verified state or keep live state that cannot be written down, and record why on the issue. At 400k, or after any compaction, they hand off. A handoff is an issue comment (state, next step, open decisions with reasons), and the next session starts by priming, e.g. "prime, then continue <issue> from its handoff".
2. The issue tool is beads_rust (`br`) when it is available.

Why: the user decided on 2026-10-18, after researching compaction and context rot, that mid-issue auto-compaction is the main failure to avoid. Evidence used: Anthropic documents context rot (accuracy and recall fall as tokens grow) and does not give Opus 4.7+ live token counts. Chroma found every tested model worse on a ~113k full history than on the focused ~300 tokens. Du et al. 2510.05381 found 13.9-85% drops with perfect retrieval. The CAT paper found a ReAct SWE agent declines after ~60 rounds while a ~35k condensed agent keeps improving. LangWatch (873 compactions) found 2.37x more user corrections after a compaction, ~8k tokens of context actually used per step, ~94% of useful file re-reference coverage within 200k, and failing cycles below ~110k.

Design: amend the existing owners. AP-SESSION-001 already owns compaction continuity; AP-PLAN-001 already owns "use the issue tool". Rejected: window percentages, which are meaningless across 200k and 1M windows (the user first proposed 50%/70%, then a 25-50% soft zone; the agreed marks are 100k/180k/250k/400k). Rejected: a new protocol, or a host-specific hook in Starcompass. Measuring context use is host tooling; the protocol says to estimate conservatively when the host reports nothing.

Budget: the greenfield + terminal-engine canonical cap was full (13,100). The user asked for these rules, so the cap rises to fit them rather than trimming other rules.

Scope: two protocol wordings, behavior trials, versions and index, budget constant and docs, CHANGELOG, LOC, self-adoption. Consumer re-imports are separate.

Acceptance:
1. AP-SESSION-001 states the token marks and handoff; AP-PLAN-001 names br.
2. docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md gains cases whose input does not disclose the rules, and they pass on the candidate.
3. version-check, index, validate, the full repository checks, and the byte budgets pass.
4. CHANGELOG, README budget and LOC, DESIGN, and the exact-pinned self-adoption are reconciled.

title: Make Starcompass the Claude-primary home of the owner's skills
description:
## Why

The owner (2026-10-18): "lets put my skills in starcompass. enough split brain madness", and "we can say starcompass is claude-focused".

Today the owner's working rules are split across three places: Starcompass protocols (rendered into each project's AGENTS.md), a personal skills repo (https://github.com/luccahuguet/skills, 16 skills, linked into ~/.claude/skills and ~/.codex/skills by its install.sh), and per-project overlays. That split surfaced while planning the converge review loop (machines_vs_aliens mva-snu): a project rule saying "finish through `converge`" would name a skill that exists only on the owner's machine, and Starcompass couldn't impose it.

Current state: Starcompass is Codex-focused. README sizes AGENTS.md around Codex's 32 KiB project-document loader; its two skills are "Codex skills" validated with Codex's skill checker; docs/DESIGN.md "Skill boundary" says only protocol-applying skills live here, and that general writing, UI, review, opinion and repository-management skills "belong elsewhere".

## Owner decisions (2026-10-18)

- **Starcompass holds the owner's skills.** All 16 skills from luccahuguet/skills move here, plus its install script. This reverses DESIGN.md's skill boundary.
- **Claude-primary.** Protocols and skills are written for Claude Code and may name its mechanisms (subagents, skills, hooks). AGENTS.md stays readable by Codex, and Codex stays a supported tool, notably as converge's second-model reviewer. Codex's loader size and conventions stop driving the design. Rejected: Claude-only (it would demote converge's Codex reviewer to a guest tool).
- **Import with history, then archive the old repo.** The skills come in with their git history (3 commits), and luccahuguet/skills is archived with a README pointing here. Rejected: copying without history and deleting the old repo (it loses history and breaks links).
- **converge is built here**, not in the personal repo (decisions on machines_vs_aliens mva-snu: a fresh subagent fix pass per round until a pass changes nothing; Codex for deep-review beads or diffs over about 200 changed source lines; any code, test or script change ends with at least one clean pass, and docs- or planning-only work skips the loop).

## Children

1. Declare Starcompass Claude-primary: README, DESIGN (skill boundary, host wording, the size-budget rationale) and the skill validation path.
2. Import the 16 skills and the install script with history, relink the installed skills to Starcompass, and archive luccahuguet/skills.
3. Build the converge skill (after 2, since it builds on fresh-pass).
4. Propose the review-convergence outcome rule as a protocol in the profiles (after 3 and its trial in machines_vs_aliens mva-snu).

## Coordination

The open epic ap-jo9 (trim the greenfield canonical block, lower byte caps) and child 4 pull in opposite directions on rendered size. Child 4 checks ap-jo9's state and byte caps first.

## Acceptance

- Starcompass's docs say it's Claude-primary and that it holds the owner's skills.
- All 16 skills and converge live in starcompass/skills and are installed from here; luccahuguet/skills is archived with a pointer.
- The review-convergence rule is proposed (and, if the owner accepts, adopted) as a protocol.

title: Build the converge review-loop skill
description:
Parent epic ap-bak holds the owner's decisions (2026-10-18) and the evidence; read it first.

## Outcome

A `converge` skill in starcompass/skills that finishes implementation through a recursive review loop, as decided on machines_vs_aliens mva-snu (read its body and comments; they hold the full decisions and evidence).

## Scope

- The main session is a thin orchestrator. It primes on the bead, then (optional for small beads) spawns an implementer subagent with the bead, handoff, repo rules and the project's build and run limits.
- Each review round is a brand-new subagent that reviews and fixes, using the owner's prompt verbatim ("take a fresh eyes and simplification pass over this diff, fixing anything you find"), then runs the checks. It sees the bead and the diff, not earlier rounds. A round that changes nothing means converged (AP-PROOF-001 v9: nits don't block; text-only fixes restart a review at most twice). After about 5 rounds without converging, stop and report what keeps changing.
- Codex joins for beads labelled `deep-review` or diffs over about 200 changed source lines; convergence then needs a clean pass from both. Codex runs unattended with stdin closed and a timeout (AP-PROOF-001).
- Scope by bead size: any change to code, tests or scripts ends with at least one clean pass; docs- and planning-only work skips the loop.
- Only one round builds at a time; parallel rounds only read. Respect each project's build limits (its README or AGENTS.md).
- Records each round's changes, the final clean pass and the checks on the bead. A bead whose acceptance needs owner sign-off stays open.
- Recommended: `fresh-pass` stays a single pass that converge calls each round; remove its "repeat once" step so converge owns looping.

## Acceptance

- converge is installed from Starcompass. Agent behavior is proven by machines_vs_aliens mva-snu's trial (converge on mva-su2.2's commit 2c8b8a9 in a fresh session), not by the skill's structure (AP-TEST-001).

title: Propose the review-convergence rule as a protocol
description:
Parent epic ap-bak holds the owner's decisions (2026-10-18) and the evidence.

## Why

Owner decision (2026-10-18, ap-bak): implementation isn't finished until a fresh reviewer finds
nothing more to fix. Owner, 2026-10-19: "im not remembering to use the converge skill" and "if we
add instructions to 'always use the converge skill' then i think the agents will use it". The
rule must make the agent run the loop, not the owner. AP-PROOF-001 already defines convergence
("Review changes require another pass; convergence needs a full clean pass"), but no rule says
when a review must happen.

## Decisions (owner, 2026-10-19)

- The rule names the converge skill explicitly: agents act on a named skill more reliably than
  on an outcome they must map to one. Starcompass is Claude-primary, so protocols may name its
  mechanisms (README).
- It also states the outcome host-neutrally, so Codex and other hosts know what is required.
- "Always" covers code, tests and scripts; docs- and planning-only work is exempt, as converge
  already exempts it.
- Home: an AP-PROOF-001 revision (recommended), since it already owns convergence
  (AP-OWNERSHIP-001). A new protocol only if the text cannot fit there.
- Subagent authorization is settled by AP-SESSION-001 v4 (ap-7xr): subagents are authorized
  unless the user or local rules say otherwise. No extra text needed.
- Enforcement is prose first. A deterministic Stop hook is a later backstop only if the trial
  shows agents skipping converge. Rejected: an LLM-review Stop hook (fires on every turn, each
  block costs a full turn, duplicates converge; LLM judges flag correct code, arXiv 2603.00539).
- The machines_vs_aliens mva-snu trial is dropped ("forget machines vs aliens"). This bead's
  trial is also converge's behavior proof (ap-bak.3 closed without one).

## Draft (about 250 bytes)

> A change to code, tests, or scripts is finished only when a fresh reviewer that did not write
> it makes a full pass that changes nothing. In Claude Code, use the converge skill. Docs-only
> and planning-only work is exempt.

## Scope

In scope: protocols/AP-PROOF-001.md (version bump), protocols/index.json via `index`,
docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md (new BT-PROOF-008), README/CHANGELOG/docs/DESIGN.md text about
AP-PROOF-001, the README LOC scorecard.

Out of scope: skills/converge and skills/fresh-pass (the review-sharpening bead under ap-bak),
profiles (AP-PROOF-001 is already in all five), hooks, consumer repositories.

## Acceptance

- AP-PROOF-001 states the rule; the owner accepts the wording.
- BT-PROOF-008 passes on the candidate: in a fixture repo with a small code bead, an agent told
  only to implement the bead finishes through converge (at least one fresh review round)
  without being asked; a docs-only variant runs no review loop.
- version-check, index, validate and the full checks pass; no profile exceeds its cap.

## Verification

- ap-jo9's per-change procedure: `version-check --base HEAD`, `index`, `validate`, cargo fmt,
  check, test (byte budgets), clippy, both skill validators, `git diff --check`.
- BT-PROOF-008 run headless and isolated as recorded on ap-b5b.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the rule pushes a profile over its byte cap; report the sizes.
- Stop if the trial shows the agent does not invoke converge: record it and ask the owner about
  the deterministic Stop-hook backstop.

## Maintenance Notes

- ap-jo9.7 lowers the byte caps after this lands.
- Self-adoption follows the two-revision bootstrap (AGENTS.md).

title: Sharpen converge rounds: leftovers check, cited findings, new-surface report
description:
Parent epic ap-bak holds the owner's skills decisions.

## Why

Leftovers after a change and checks that cannot fail are the owner's most frequent code-level
failures (survey of the owner's repos, 2026-10-19), and fresh-context review is what caught
them. A concrete brief makes each converge round catch them more reliably with fewer false
positives. Owner accepted this plan on 2026-10-19.

## Evidence

- Leftovers: eon 80db4ff then 45f051a (single-field struct); zellij-pane-orchestrator 58b2937
  (no-op `LayoutFamily::next` plus a test asserting it), 7c8ce6c (a generic with one use);
  eon beads eon-tool-popups-e13.2 and eon-pxn.5 (always-true parameters), eon-omq (13 unused
  derives), eon-pxn.3 (single-call wrappers); bend-orbit 6d902934 (`Result` on infallible code).
- A check that cannot fail: eon b1c374e (`! grep` absence checks never tripped errexit).
- LLM judges mark correct code non-compliant, and asking them to explain or propose fixes makes
  it worse (arXiv 2603.00539); adopted AI review suggestions add more complexity than human ones
  (arXiv 2603.15911).
- skills/fresh-pass/SKILL.md is the single pass every converge round runs;
  skills/converge/SKILL.md owns the loop.

## Scope

In scope: skills/fresh-pass/SKILL.md, skills/converge/SKILL.md, and one new script under
skills/converge/scripts/.

Out of scope: protocols, hooks, any blocking gate, the loop's existing decisions (round shape,
Codex threshold, caps).

## Changes

1. fresh-pass leftovers check: when the diff removes or narrows a concept, delete what existed
   only for it: a single-field struct, a single-call wrapper, an always-true parameter, an unused
   derive, `Result` on infallible code, a generic with one instantiation, a test asserting a
   no-op.
2. fresh-pass questions, answered yes or no: does this have a second caller today? Is this
   option ever set? Does an existing helper or the standard library already do this (name its
   path)? Every finding cites `path:line`. Simplification fixes only delete or inline; bug fixes
   are unrestricted.
3. fresh-pass: a new negative or absence check must be shown failing on a seeded violation
   before it is trusted.
4. converge: before the first round, the orchestrator runs the script against the base. It lists
   added dependencies (Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml, requirements*.txt) and added
   `pub`/`export` lines, and the list goes to every round as review input: each item is
   justified or removed. It is not a gate.

Rejected: LLM review in a Stop hook; hard diff-size caps; clippy `single_call_fn`,
`cognitive_complexity` or whole-repo jscpd as gates (`single_call_fn` fired 20 times on
Starcompass's ~2,950 LOC); a reviewer persona (Ponytail issue #502).

## Acceptance

- Both skills carry the changes. In a temporary repo, the script reports an added dependency and
  an added `pub fn`, and prints nothing for a diff without them.
- Behavior (AP-TEST-001): in an isolated agent, fresh-pass on a fixture diff that leaves a
  single-field struct after removing a field deletes the struct and cites `path:line`.

## Verification

- `claude plugin validate --strict skills`, the Codex quick_validate loop from AGENTS.md, and
  `git diff --check` pass.
- The script check above. The script is code, so the change finishes through converge.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the brief makes fresh-pass longer than about 70 lines; cut instead.
- Stop if the behavior trial fails twice for the same reason after a wording fix.
acceptance_criteria: fresh-pass carries the leftovers check, yes/no questions with path:line citations, delete-or-inline-only simplification fixes, code added only to fix a defect, and seeded-failure proof for new absence checks; converge passes a new-dependency and new-public-symbol report to every round; the script and an isolated fresh-pass trial pass; skill validators pass.
close_reason: fresh-pass carries the leftovers check, yes/no questions with path:line citations and delete-or-inline-only fixes; converge feeds the new-surface report to every round; script proof, isolated trial and skill validators pass; converged in 3 rounds

title: Render canonical protocol text to an optional separate consumer file
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-16 (from Eon `eon-slim-agent-instructions-jr9k`): let a consumer keep canonical
protocol text out of the always-loaded `AGENTS.md`. Eon's root plus `orbit/AGENTS.md` reached 32,742
of Codex's 32,768-byte chain limit.

## Contract
- Consumer: a repository rendering an import.
- Trigger: `render --protocol-file NAME` (NAME relative to `--agents-out`'s directory, plain names).
- Result: canonical protocol text goes to NAME under a generated header; `AGENTS.md` keeps the
import record, exceptions and local rules, and tells agents to read NAME before planning,
changing or reviewing work. The manifest records `protocol_file`. `check` compares NAME with the
pinned source; `check-consumer` checks its header, rejects protocol text inlined in `AGENTS.md`,
and rejects an escaping path. Only `AGENTS.md` files count toward the chain limit.
- Without the flag every output is byte-identical to before.
- The self-contained invariant becomes "self-contained within the consumer".

## Rejected
A per-protocol summary list in `AGENTS.md` (titles are not in the manifest, so `check-consumer`
could not verify it; the import table already lists IDs). Remote includes (break offline use).

## Acceptance
fmt, check, tests (new `protocol_file_moves_canonical_text_out_of_agents`), clippy, skill
validation, `check-consumer`, and an Eon render that passes `check` at the new commit.

title: Reject symlinked parents for nested and protocol-file outputs
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-16: track this; found by the ap-ca8 review.

## Problem
`render` validates `--nested` directories and `--protocol-file` lexically (plain relative names, no
`..`), but writes through a symlinked parent. With `ext -> ../outside`, `--protocol-file ext/P.md`
created `outside/P.md`; `--nested orbit` with `orbit` symlinked outside writes
`outside/AGENTS.md` the same way. Reproduced at aa96764. Impact is low (fixed generated content,
operator-chosen names), but the README's "cannot let an output escape" reading invites the stronger
assumption.

## Contract (provisional)
Before any write, render rejects a nested directory or protocol-file path whose components under the
consumer base include a symlink. The same check runs where checks read those files.

## Shape
One shared helper used by both features: walk each component under the base with
`symlink_metadata` and reject symlinks. Optionally also reject a protocol path that is an existing
directory before any write (today that fails with EISDIR after nested files are written).

## Acceptance
Focused tests for a symlinked nested directory and a symlinked protocol-file parent; README states
the rule; outputs without symlinks are unchanged.

title: Decide: cite the protocol ID behind each changed decision
description:
## Decision

Should agents name the protocol ID behind each decision it changed? For
example: "AP-MINIMAL-001: reused the existing helper instead of adding a
module."

Recommendation: trial first, and adopt only if citations track real decisions
rather than being added after the fact.

## Why

Source: pstack (`cursor/plugins`, `pstack/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md`,
"Non-negotiables", read 2026-10-21): "name each principle that shaped a
decision and the specific choice it changed. Cite only principles whose leaf
SKILL.md you read this session." An open pstack issue, `cursor/plugins#726`,
reports that in Claude Code it cites principles without reading them.

In pstack this is weak, because principle names are unversioned and change
almost weekly (for example `cursor/plugins` #633, #634, #702). A citation in a
committed record goes stale. Starcompass IDs are permanent and versioned, and
the consumer manifest pins the exact text. A citation like "AP-MINIMAL-001 v7"
stays exact, even in a commit message.

The value: reasoning a reviewer can check against the diff, and data on which
protocols actually change decisions. That data is useful under the byte caps.
The risks: citations added after the decision, too many of them, and the fact
that a citation is still the agent's own word, not proof.

## Options

- One protocol sentence: "When a protocol changes a decision, name its ID and
  the choice it changed." Its home would be AP-PROOF-001 or AP-REFERENCE-001.
- Ask for citations only in skill reports, such as converge round reports and
  handoffs. This costs no protocol bytes.
- No change.

## If adopted

1. Add a behavior-trial case to `docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md`. Run the same task
   with and without the sentence. Score whether each citation matches a choice
   visible in the diff, and whether the choices differ between the two runs.
2. Pick the protocol or the skill-report option from the result. Keep it within
   the byte caps (`src/starcompass/render.rs:358`).
3. Do the usual version bump, `index`, and `validate`, the full verification,
   and the `CHANGELOG.md` entry.
close_reason: Rejected: 0/4 runs cited IDs with the sentence; no protocol change

title: Compact canonical protocols below the consumer instruction budget
description:
## Contract

Starcompass must keep each shipped profile's canonical/import section self-contained and offline-capable while fitting within 12,288 bytes when rendered with no exceptions and an empty local overlay. This leaves at least 2 KiB of headroom when the current largest Yazelix consumer overlay (Orbit, 17,690 bytes) is combined with the canonical rules under Codex's default 32,768-byte project-instruction limit. The reduction must preserve the non-obvious scope, ownership, safety, evidence, planning, and proof behavior of the selected protocols. A focused repository test must fail with the profile name, actual byte count, and limit if canonical growth breaks the budget; do not add a new public command or reject a consumer solely because its locally owned overlay exceeds a host-specific limit.

## Why

Starcompass is intentionally the canonical rule source for the Yazelix Eon stack. The stack should keep consuming it; an Eon-specific fork or optional remote include would create drift and violate the self-contained design. The current canonical payload is nevertheless large enough to make a real consumer exceed Codex's default project-document cap, silently omitting repository-local rules near the end of `AGENTS.md`.

Effort: M. Risk: MED because shortening agent instructions can change behavior even when structural checks remain green. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `README.md:28-36` defines one complete rendered `AGENTS.md` containing canonical rules and the consumer overlay, available without Starcompass or network access.
- `docs/DESIGN.md:75-85` explicitly rejects remote inclusion and keeps the generated import record auditable.
- `protocols/AP-MINIMAL-001.md:22-27` already treats durable agent context as lifecycle cost and rejects duplicated or generic policy.
- `src/starcompass.rs:658-728` selects and de-duplicates profile protocols; `src/starcompass.rs:738-831` renders the import record, every selected canonical body, then the repository-local overlay.
- At Starcompass revision `bcc782f645c8c1d106992c69473e8fd6b78c5ebf`, the self-adopted `greenfield` canonical/import section is 17,378 bytes.
- Orbit's rendered `greenfield + terminal-engine` import is 35,313 bytes: 17,623 canonical/import bytes plus a 17,690-byte local overlay. With no local `project_doc_max_bytes` override, that exceeds Codex's default 32 KiB limit by 2,545 bytes and can omit the final local Git, Beads, LOC, and verification rules.
- Venus's current `greenfield` import is 21,937 bytes: 13,509 canonical/import bytes plus an 8,428-byte local overlay.
- Official Codex guidance documents a default 32 KiB combined project-instruction limit and recommends concise or nested guidance: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md#how-codex-discovers-guidance

## Reference Gate

Before editing, record the inspected Starcompass revision, the current Orbit and Venus manifests and byte measurements, and the current official Codex project-instruction limit. Preserve these decisions:

- Keep canonical rules self-contained; detailed rationale may move to existing README/design documentation only when it is not required to act safely or correctly.
- Compact the Starcompass-owned wording instead of raising every user's Codex limit, reordering local rules ahead of canonical rules, creating an Eon-specific protocol fork/profile, or loading canonical rules remotely/on demand.
- Keep repository-local overlays owned by consumers. This bead budgets canonical profile output; it does not rewrite Orbit, Venus, or Eon policy.
- Do not rely on structural checks alone for semantic preservation; use the applicable isolated behavior trials.

## Scope

In scope:

- Audit all active `protocols/AP-*.md` for duplicated rationale, repeated generic agent capability, and wording that can be made shorter without weakening normative behavior.
- Prioritize the largest shared protocols, especially `AP-MINIMAL-001`, `AP-PLAN-001`, `AP-REFERENCE-001`, `AP-CONTRACT-001`, `AP-PROOF-001`, `AP-SCOPE-001`, and `AP-GIT-001`.
- Increment every changed protocol version, regenerate `protocols/index.json`, and retain all permanent protocol IDs and profile membership unless separate user approval changes scope.
- Add one focused Rust regression check covering every shipped profile's exact canonical/import byte count with empty exceptions and overlay, capped at 12,288 bytes.
- Update README/design wording, CHANGELOG, and the README LOC scorecard for the accepted protocol and proof behavior.
- Complete Starcompass's documented two-revision self-adoption flow after the protocol-bearing revision is accepted.

Out of scope:

- Consumer repository edits or upgrades.
- New protocols, profiles, exceptions, dependencies, public CLI options, remote includes, runtime fetching, tokenization libraries, model-specific token estimates, or a second compact rendering format.
- Reducing consumer-owned overlays or weakening safety, scope authority, ownership, evidence, planning, proof, Git, or exception requirements.

## Implementation Notes

1. Record the baseline canonical/import byte count for each profile using the existing deterministic renderer.
2. Remove repetition and demote explanation before removing any normative requirement. Prefer prose reduction over renderer complexity.
3. Add the smallest internal helper/test needed to measure canonical/import bytes; keep rendering and validation ownership in `src/starcompass.rs`.
4. Bump changed protocol versions, run the history gate, regenerate the index, and update current-state docs.
5. Run the behavior trials corresponding to every materially changed protocol; at minimum cover BT-SCOPE-001, BT-PLAN-001, BT-REFERENCE-001, and both BT-PROOF cases if those protocols change.
6. Commit and verify the protocol-bearing revision, then render self-adoption from a clean checkout pinned to that exact revision as documented.

## Acceptance

- Every individual shipped profile renders a canonical/import section of at most 12,288 bytes with empty exceptions and local overlay.
- The regression test reports profile, actual bytes, and limit on failure.
- Orbit's current 17,690-byte overlay plus the accepted `terminal-engine` canonical/import output totals at most 30,720 bytes, preserving at least 2,048 bytes below the Codex default cap.
- Rendered files remain self-contained, deterministic, source-pinned, exception-aware, and byte-for-byte checkable.
- Relevant isolated behavior trials reach the same expected conclusions before and after the wording reduction, with revision, model/host, and result recorded in the Bead.
- No protocol ID, profile, dependency, or public command is added.
- Starcompass self-adoption is refreshed through the documented two-revision process.

## Verification

- `cargo run --locked --quiet -- version-check --base <protocol-baseline>` exits 0 before index regeneration.
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -- index` followed by `cargo run --locked --quiet -- validate` exits 0.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0.
- Both bundled skill validation commands from `AGENTS.md` exit 0.
- The source-backed self-import check runs from the exact manifest-pinned checkout and exits 0.
- `git diff --check` exits 0 and the README LOC scorecard matches tracked project files.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if meeting the byte budget would require removing a safety-critical or behavior-changing requirement rather than shortening duplicated/explanatory wording.
- Stop and request user direction if an existing profile must lose a protocol, a new compact format or profile appears necessary, or a consumer overlay must change.
- Stop if representative behavior trials regress even though structural checks pass.

## Maintenance Notes

The 12 KiB value is a canonical profile budget, not a claim about GPT-5.6 Sol's model context window. It exists to leave predictable room inside the current Codex project-document loader cap. Future host-limit changes may justify revisiting the number with measured consumer evidence; do not add configuration until a real supported consumer needs it.
notes:
Reference gate verified before implementation edits on 2026-08-06. Starcompass baseline is bcc782f645c8c1d106992c69473e8fd6b78c5ebf. Empty-exception, empty-overlay canonical/import byte counts from its deterministic renderer are fork 17,929; greenfield 17,378; orchestrator 19,686; release 20,081; terminal-engine 19,692; and greenfield plus terminal-engine 19,706. Orbit currently pins 95c29fa76a971726b65e1d1dc06c518d525c46a2 with greenfield plus terminal-engine: AGENTS.md 35,313 bytes, canonical/import 17,623, rendered local suffix 17,690, raw overlay 17,663. Venus currently pins c3e316f1e7ca2d9fe850b16e7af8140ad9627620 with greenfield: AGENTS.md 21,937 bytes, canonical/import 13,509, rendered local suffix 8,428, raw overlay 8,401. The current official Codex manual page Custom instructions with AGENTS.md states that Codex stops adding project instruction files at project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB by default, and recommends raising the limit or splitting instructions across nested directories. Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md#how-codex-discovers-guidance. Accepted design keeps canonical rules self-contained and compacts Starcompass prose; it does not raise consumer limits, reorder local rules, fork profiles, fetch remote text, or edit consumers.

User-approved compaction filter: use GPT-5.6 Sol as the current behavioral oracle. Retain canonical wording only when it protects a demonstrated model weakness, a high-cost safety or evidence boundary, or a repository-specific workflow the model cannot infer. Remove generic good-agent advice that the model already follows. Keep protocol wording publisher-neutral and record trial evidence rather than encoding model-specific claims.

Clean GPT-5.6 Sol controls used Codex CLI 0.146.1, model gpt-5.6-sol, OpenAI provider, reasoning effort none, Linux x86_64, 2026-08-06, isolated CODEX_HOME with no personal skills, plugins, AGENTS.md, or repository rules. BT-SCOPE-001 passed without protocols: diagnosis remained non-mutating. BT-CONTRACT-001 passed: only status --json was added. BT-PLAN-001 failed: the agent did not discover the repository's hidden Beads state or designated issue tool and asked for a GitHub repository instead of creating the approved local batch. BT-REFERENCE-001 passed: it inspected the implementation and kept license actors and uses scoped. BT-PROOF-001 passed: it profiled before editing, retained the old parser as a correctness oracle, compared repeated same-workload samples, and reported only the measured result. BT-PROOF-002 failed its convergence condition: it found and fixed the bug and simplification, ran checks, then declared completion without a fresh review pass over the revised state. These controls justify explicit planning-tool and convergence wording; the other protocols retain only terse high-cost boundary reminders.

Accepted protocol-bearing revision 2077f8664ed99092a1b08683d46e9296503012e2. Exact empty-exception, empty-overlay canonical/import bytes from that clean checkout: fork 11,169; greenfield 10,755; orchestrator 12,268; release 12,190; terminal-engine 12,267; greenfield plus terminal-engine 12,281. Orbit's measured 17,690-byte rendered local suffix therefore totals 29,971 bytes, leaving 2,797 bytes below 32 KiB. All five individual profiles satisfy the 12,288-byte limit; the Orbit combination satisfies its 13,030-byte canonical limit. Compared with baseline, individual reductions range from 6,209 to 7,891 bytes.

Post-change behavior trials used the exact source revision above with Codex CLI 0.146.1, gpt-5.6-sol, OpenAI provider, reasoning effort none, Linux x86_64, 2026-08-06, and an isolated CODEX_HOME without personal skills or plugins. BT-SCOPE-001 passed without mutation. BT-CONTRACT-001 added only status --json, preserved text status, and retained invalid-argument failure. BT-PLAN-001 discovered the hidden Beads repository, initialized it through the CLI, and created exactly three open, unclaimed, independent issues without implementation. BT-REFERENCE-001 inspected the permitted implementation, reported same-directory temporary write, file fsync, atomic replace, cleanup, and the directory-fsync durability caveat. BT-PROOF-001 established the parser contract, measured multiple candidates on the same 10,000-record workload, retained the old parser as oracle, reported distributions, rejected slower shapes, and documented a measured environment-specific result. BT-PROOF-002 fixed the lower-bound bug, explicitly ran the required post-fix convergence pass, and declared clean only after that pass. The malformed first BT-CONTRACT invocation was interrupted and discarded before assessment; only the safely quoted rerun is evidence.

title: Add a session-continuity protocol for context compaction
description:
## Chosen outcome — user, 2026-10-14
"Save it to Starcompass." Make the session rules Lucca adopted for Eon a canonical protocol, so every consumer importing greenfield or fork gets them.

## Contract
A new protocol, AP-SESSION-001 version 1, agent-neutral and host-neutral, with no thresholds or tool names:
- Treat compaction as lossy.
- Write each user decision to its durable owner when it is made.
- Reread the active issue after compaction.
- After a compacted session, start the next issue fresh.
- Within an issue, a second compaction or lost context triggers a handoff (state, next step, open decisions) and a new session.
- Prefer a clean-break restart over compaction, and start large issues fresh when most of the context is already used.

Evidence:
- Research on compaction: side constraints are lost, user corrections spike after a compaction, and loss compounds across rounds.
- The Claude Opus 5.5 system card §8.10: ProgramBench 91.2% with contexts up to 1M and no compaction, so long uncompacted contexts work.

## Profiles and budget
Add it to greenfield and fork. orchestrator, release and terminal-engine each sit within 8 bytes of the 12,288-byte budget, so they stay unchanged; a consumer gets the protocol through greenfield. The greenfield + terminal-engine combination must stay within its 13,030-byte budget. Rejected: raising budgets, which is a separate policy decision.

## Acceptance
- version-check, index and validate pass.
- Tests pass with 22 protocols, and every budget test passes.
- README, CHANGELOG and the LOC scorecard are updated.
- Self-adoption is re-rendered in the follow-up revision.

Proof: version-check --base HEAD, index and validate (22 protocols, 5 profiles) pass. cargo test --locked passes 19 unit + 4 CLI tests, including both budget tests; the catalog and CLI counts moved from 21 to 22. clippy -D warnings, fmt --check and git diff --check are clean. Rendered sizes: greenfield 11,407 and fork 11,821 of 12,288; greenfield + terminal-engine 12,931 of 13,030. orchestrator, release and terminal-engine are unchanged at 12,280-12,283, which is why the protocol is not in them. title: Decide: observable facts are not the user's question (AP-SCOPE-001)
description:
## Decision

Should AP-SCOPE-001 say that a question whose answer the agent could observe by
running something is not the user's to answer?

Recommendation: adopt, after a behavior trial shows it changes behavior.
Proposed wording, about 90 bytes: "A question you could answer by running
something is not the user's; run it."

## Why

Source: pstack (`cursor/plugins`, `pstack/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md`, the
`AskQuestion` trigger, read 2026-10-21). Before asking "which approach?", pstack
asks whether the answer is a fact the agent could observe: behavior, timing,
layout, output, or performance. If it is, the agent builds a throwaway
prototype and lets the result decide. It asks only for a product or preference
call that no experiment can settle.

AP-SCOPE-001 says "stop when a missing scope choice would materially change the
result" and "recommend and justify an answer to every choice". Neither tells the
agent to settle an observable fork itself, so agents still stop on questions
they could answer.

## Options

- Add the sentence to AP-SCOPE-001. Recommended: AP-SCOPE-001 already owns when
  to stop and ask.
- Add it to AP-REFERENCE-001 as evidence before code shape. A weaker home,
  because the failure is asking, not shaping.
- No change. Arguably "scope choice" already excludes facts, but that is
  implicit.

## Constraints

- `regular` measures 11,172 bytes against an 11,400 cap
  (`src/starcompass/render.rs:358`, README budget table). The sentence fits
  only by trimming elsewhere or raising the cap, and the cap leaves room under
  Codex's 32 KiB limit.
- A protocol change bumps AP-SCOPE-001's version and takes the two-revision
  self-adoption (`AGENTS.md`, "Bootstrap Self-Adoption").

## If adopted

1. Add a case to `docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md` (for example `BT-SCOPE-002`). Give
   the agent a "which approach is faster?" fork that a ten-line benchmark
   settles, and score whether it asks or measures. Run it with and without the
   sentence (AP-TEST-001).
2. If the sentence changes the result, edit `protocols/AP-SCOPE-001.md`, then
   run `version-check --base HEAD`, `index`, and `validate`, plus the full
   verification in `AGENTS.md`.
3. Update `CHANGELOG.md` and the README budget table.
close_reason: Rejected: BT-SCOPE-002 passes without the sentence; AP-SCOPE-001 unchanged

title: Trim the greenfield canonical block for directive count and clarity
description:
## Why

The greenfield canonical/import section is 11,964 bytes (measured at c88a6b2, about 3k tokens). Its token cost is small, but it packs many directives into compressed slash-list prose. Instruction-following degrades as the number of directives grows, and models favor the ones that come first (IFScale, arXiv 2507.11538). Context files make agents do more of whatever they say, at real cost (ETH Zurich AGENTS.md study, arXiv 2602.11988). The byte budgets pushed wording toward compression rather than removal. User decision, 2026-10-18: cut the rules that rarely apply in a small new project and remove overlaps, aiming to cut greenfield by about a sixth (the listed cuts add up to roughly 2 KB), and prove with behavior trials that nothing regresses.

## Acceptance

- No profile grows past its current cap; the greenfield size is whatever the children leave (owner, 2026-10-19: the 10,000-byte target is dropped).
- Every behavior trial in docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md passes on the final revision for the protocols it names.
- Niche rules moved out of greenfield still exist in a protocol that some profile includes, or were removed by an explicit recorded decision.

## Planned children (in order)

1. Split performance claims and the proof-phase vocabulary out of AP-PROOF-001.
2. Split the license-interpretation paragraph out of AP-REFERENCE-001.
3. Move the Ponytail paragraph out of AP-MINIMAL-001.
4. Remove AP-CI-001 from the greenfield profile.
5. Remove overlap among AP-SCOPE-001, AP-CONTRACT-001, AP-MINIMAL-001 and AP-OWNERSHIP-001.
6. Remove canonical repeats from Starcompass's own .agent-protocols.local.md.
7. Lower the byte caps to the new sizes, self-adopt, and re-run the full trial suite.

Children are chained with blocks dependencies because each one touches protocols/index.json, CHANGELOG.md and the README LOC scorecard. Run them one at a time.

## Per-change procedure (every child that edits protocols or profiles)

- Bump the version of every protocol file you change (Protocol IDs are permanent; a new rule gets a new ID such as AP-PERF-001). Run `cargo run --locked --quiet -- version-check --base HEAD`, then `index`, then `validate`.
- Run the full checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, `cargo test --locked` (includes the byte-budget test in src/starcompass/render.rs), `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, both skill validators listed in AGENTS.md, and `git diff --check`.
- Measure each profile as ap-b5b did: render it with an empty overlay from a clean commit; the canonical/import size is the rendered AGENTS.md bytes minus the local-rules section. Record the sizes on the child.
- Run the behavior trials that name the changed protocols, headless and isolated, as recorded on ap-b5b (Claude Code `claude -p`, stream-json, acceptEdits with a narrow allowlist, stdin closed, timeout 600; the agent gets only the Input text and a fixture built from the case's Fixture summary). Move or rename a trial's `Protocols:` line when its rule moves.
- Update CHANGELOG.md and the README LOC scorecard, and README/docs/DESIGN.md wherever they describe the changed rule.
- Do not self-adopt in each child; child 7 renders the self-adoption once.
close_reason: All 10 children closed; acceptance met: profiles within per-profile caps, all 19 trials pass on 6c40032, moved rules live in AP-LICENSE-001 and AP-PERF-001

title: Split performance claims and proof phases out of AP-PROOF-001
description:
## Why

AP-PROOF-001 (v8, 1,134 bytes) is the densest greenfield protocol. Two parts rarely apply to a small new project: performance claims (measured bottleneck, fixed workload, baseline, oracle, distribution) and the proof-phase vocabulary (proposed, implemented, mechanically verified, dogfooded, accepted, promoted), which mainly serves release channels.

## Evidence

- protocols/AP-PROOF-001.md, first paragraph: proof records and the six phases.
- protocols/AP-PROOF-001.md, last paragraph: the performance-claim rule.
- docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md: BT-PROOF-001 tests performance claims; BT-PROOF-004 involves AP-DELIVERY-001.

## Scope

In scope: protocols/AP-PROOF-001.md; one new protocol for performance claims (recommended ID AP-PERF-001); profiles/*.json membership; docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md Protocols lines; CHANGELOG.md, README.md and docs/DESIGN.md text about AP-PROOF-001.

Out of scope: the core proof rules (highest changed boundary, complete suite once per unchanged candidate, rerun after material change, bounded unattended runs and waits, review convergence). Their meaning must not change.

## Acceptance

- AP-PROOF-001 keeps only the core rules in plain sentences, with no slash-lists.
- Performance claims live in the new protocol, included in terminal-engine and release (recommended; record the choice and reason if different).
- The phase vocabulary moves into AP-DELIVERY-001 or AP-PROMOTION-001 if they rely on it; otherwise it is removed, with that decision recorded here.
- Greenfield shrinks by at least 350 bytes.

## Implementation Notes

1. Check AP-DELIVERY-001 and AP-PROMOTION-001 for phase terms before moving them.
2. Create the new protocol file with frontmatter `version: 1`, add it to the chosen profiles, and run the per-change procedure from the epic.
3. Point BT-PROOF-001's Protocols line at the new protocol.

## Verification

- The epic's per-change procedure passes.
- BT-PROOF-001 through BT-PROOF-007 pass on the candidate (BT-PROOF-001 with a profile that includes the new protocol).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if AP-DELIVERY-001 or AP-PROMOTION-001 depend on the phases in a way that moving them would change their meaning; record the conflict and ask.
- Stop if a proof trial fails twice for the same reason after a wording fix.

## Maintenance Notes

- Write plain sentences rather than compressed lists; clarity is the goal, not just bytes.

title: BT-PROOF-001 fails on dc1e342: parser redesigned before measuring
description:
## Why

ap-jo9.7 reran every behavior trial on dc1e342, the revision Starcompass
self-adopts. BT-PROOF-001 failed. The agent chose and wrote a new parser
architecture from reading the code, before measuring anything, and never
profiled the bottleneck. The rubric lists "Selects an architecture from
intuition alone" as a failure condition. The ap-jo9.1 run (AP-PERF-001 v1, the
same text, in the retired `terminal-engine` profile) passed: it profiled a
fixed seeded workload before redesigning. The ap-jo9 epic needs every trial to
pass, so ap-jo9.7 is blocked on this bead.

## Evidence

- Run (2026-10-19; ap-b5b method: Claude Code 2.1.293 `claude -p`,
  claude-opus-5-5, acceptEdits, default allowlist, stdin closed, timeout 600;
  `regular` + `release` rendered at dc1e342, so AP-PERF-001 renders 13th of 16
  sections, after AP-GIT-001). The fixture code commits were fetched from
  ap-jo9.1's fixture. 565 s, 36 turns. The new parser was written at tool call
  19, and the first workload definition and baseline timing came at call 25.
  "pop(0) makes each line O(n^2)" came from reading the code, with no profile.
  What held: a differential oracle against the old parser (300k random lines,
  0 mismatches), old and new timed in the same process (median of 15 runs with
  min/max), a README table matching that output, and negative results kept.
- `protocols/AP-PERF-001.md` v1: "Performance claims need a measured
  bottleneck, a fixed workload and environment, a baseline, a correctness
  oracle, and a distribution or bound." It governs claims. It does not say to
  measure before choosing a design, which the rubric's pass condition 1
  requires ("records comparable baseline evidence before choosing a new
  design").
- What changed since the passing run: the profile composition and AP-PERF-001's
  position in it (now late, inside the `release` add-on). The run-to-run
  variance is unknown, because each verdict is one run.

## Scope

In scope:
- Diagnose whether the cause is the wording gap (claims vs. design choice),
  the protocol's position, or variance.
- Make the change the owner chooses: AP-PERF-001 wording (bump the version,
  then run `index`, `validate`, CHANGELOG, README, LOC) or BT-PROOF-001's
  rubric in `docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md`.

Out of scope:
- AP-PROOF-001 and BT-PROOF-006 (sibling bead).
- Profile order, unless the owner chooses it.
- The self-adoption: ap-jo9.7 renders it once after this bead.

## Acceptance

- The owner chooses the fix from the evidence recorded here, with the
  rejected options and their reasons on this bead.
- A fresh BT-PROOF-001 run on the candidate, rendered from `regular` +
  `release`, passes the rubric as it then stands.
- `release`, `regular + release` and `surgical + release` stay within their
  caps in `src/starcompass/render.rs`, or the owner records new ones.

## Implementation Notes

1. Variance first. Ask the owner before spending on repeated runs (BT-PROOF-001
   takes about 10 minutes per run). Diagnostic runs are not verdict runs.
2. Present the options with a recommendation: extend AP-PERF-001 to cover
   design choices made for speed (measure the bottleneck before choosing),
   narrow the rubric to claims only, or record variance.
3. Follow ap-jo9's per-change procedure for any protocol edit.

## Verification

- `cargo run --locked --quiet -- version-check --base HEAD`, `index` and
  `validate` pass if a protocol changes.
- AGENTS.md's Verification list passes, including the budget test.
- The BT-PROOF-001 verdict run, recorded with revision, fixture, host, model
  and result.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the fix needs a profile-order change. That changes every
  `release` consumer's rendered text, so the owner decides it.
- Stop if the fix pushes a profile past its cap; the owner decides caps.
