title: Remove canonical repeats from Starcompass's local overlay
description:
## Why

Starcompass's own .agent-protocols.local.md (5,513 bytes) is appended to its AGENTS.md after the canonical rules, and part of it repeats them. That adds directives to every Starcompass session without adding behavior.

## Evidence

- .agent-protocols.local.md "Core Rule" ("The user decides scope ...") repeats AP-SCOPE-001, except its Starcompass-specific list (protocol, profile, enforcement skill, compatibility surface, planning bead).
- .agent-protocols.local.md "Beads" ("Use `br` for all issue work. Do not edit `.beads/` files directly") repeats AP-PLAN-001 v12.
- "Method" steps 1-6 restate AP-CONTRACT-001, AP-REFERENCE-001, AP-DEPENDENCY-001 and AP-MINIMAL-001.

## Scope

In scope: .agent-protocols.local.md, and the rendered AGENTS.md and .agent-protocols.json produced from it.

Out of scope: canonical protocols and profiles. Keep every Starcompass-specific rule: the ownership model, bootstrap self-adoption, LOC scorecard, verification commands, `br sync --flush-only`, and working on `edge`.

## Acceptance

- The overlay keeps only rules specific to this repository; each removed passage is covered by a named canonical protocol, listed in the commit message.
- AGENTS.md is re-rendered from the currently pinned source commit and passes `check` and `check-consumer`.

## Implementation Notes

1. Remove repeats; keep the Starcompass-specific lists.
2. Render from a clean detached checkout at the source commit already pinned in .agent-protocols.json (bootstrap rule in AGENTS.md), then run `check` from that checkout and `check-consumer` locally.

## Verification

- `check` and `check-consumer` pass; `git diff --check` passes; the README LOC scorecard is updated.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a passage looks like a repeat but carries a Starcompass-specific constraint; keep it and note why.

title: AP-MINIMAL-001 v6: own the anti-bloat rules and drop Ponytail
description:
## Why

Owner, 2026-10-19: "i dont care about ponytail or not, i care about 'ponytail-like' rules being
followed", then chose to dismiss Ponytail and own the rules in Starcompass. AP-MINIMAL-001 v5
already carries Ponytail's option ladder and never-cut list. Research found four rules that the
strongest sources share and no Starcompass protocol states.

## Evidence

- Survey of the owner's repos (2026-10-19): the most frequent code-level failure is leftovers
  after a change. eon 80db4ff left a single-field `ComponentFacts` that 45f051a removed;
  zellij-pane-orchestrator 58b2937, 7c8ce6c and 2db5f41 deleted 759 lines after dfc7f31 (a
  no-op `LayoutFamily::next` with a test asserting it, a generic `TransientPaneState<Id>`).
  Fresh-context review caught them, not the rules.
- Ponytail is enabled only in Codex (~/.codex/config.toml); Claude Code never loaded it, and no
  Claude-era commit added a `ponytail:` marker.
- Ponytail 5's benchmark is author-run and measures its prose in context. An independent pre-v5
  replication (github.com/Deepusleepy/ponytail-benchmark) found about 44% less code at equal
  correctness, but robustness on unstated edge cases fell from 96.7% to about 81%.
- SlopCodeBench (arXiv 2603.24755): explicit quality guidance cuts initial verbosity by up to a
  third without changing degradation rates.
- Claude Code's and Codex's built-in prompts already say "three similar lines is better than a
  premature abstraction", no half-finished implementations, fix root causes. Do not restate them.

## Rules to add (owner accepted; write compactly, own wording)

1. Finish the change: update every caller, test, fixture, config and export it breaks.
2. No speculative structure: no single-use helper or abstraction, option, configuration, or code
   for later.
3. Edit surgically: delete what the change orphaned; report unrelated dead code instead of
   deleting it (scopes "Prefer deletion").
4. Minimal still handles implied input: empty, malformed and boundary inputs are not impossible
   cases.

Rejected: a one-liner preference (dropped a path-traversal guard in Ponytail's own 2026-06-18
run); "shortest working diff wins" (v5's "patch size only between equally correct system shapes"
is better); the lazy-dev persona (leaked into review subagents and cut their reports, Ponytail
issue #502); `shortcut:` markers (duplicate AP-PLAN issues; numeric ones went stale twice);
Ponytail's runtime, hooks and codebase map (unproven; in Claude, AGENTS.md already reaches
general-purpose subagents and survives compaction); restating host defaults.

## Scope

In scope: protocols/AP-MINIMAL-001.md (v6) and the index; README's Ponytail overlay section
(delete) and AP-MINIMAL-001 summary; docs/DESIGN.md "Upstream agent tools belong in the consumer
overlay" (drop the Ponytail naming) and its code-shape-tool sentence; CHANGELOG.md;
docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md (new BT-MINIMAL-001); the README LOC scorecard.

Out of scope: other protocols; consumer repositories (they drop the Ponytail paragraph on their
next re-render); the owner's Codex config.

## Acceptance

- AP-MINIMAL-001 v6 states the four rules, and no Starcompass file recommends Ponytail.
- BT-MINIMAL-001 passes on the candidate: a fixture task that removes a concept and invites a
  speculative option or abstraction. Pass: the smallest complete change, orphans removed,
  unrelated dead code reported but kept, implied bad input still handled, a test for new
  non-trivial logic. BT-CONTRACT-001 and BT-PROOF-002, which name AP-MINIMAL-001, still pass.
- ap-jo9's per-change procedure passes; profile sizes are recorded here.

## Implementation Notes

1. Start from the v5 text left by ap-jo9.5; fold each rule into an existing sentence where it
   overlaps instead of appending.
2. Run ap-jo9's per-change procedure.

## Open Decision

- Byte target: ap-jo9 aims for greenfield at or under 10,000 bytes. If these rules keep
  greenfield above it after ap-jo9.4 to .6, recommended: accept the measured size at ap-jo9.7,
  because these rules answer observed failures while 10,000 was a round target. The owner
  decides at ap-jo9.7.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if ap-jo9.5 changed AP-MINIMAL-001 in a way that conflicts with these rules.
- Stop if BT-MINIMAL-001 fails twice for the same reason after a wording fix.

## Maintenance Notes

- Owner follow-up after this lands: disable `ponytail@ponytail` in ~/.codex/config.toml so Codex
  sessions get one rule set; it currently injects its own SKILL.md alongside AGENTS.md.

title: BT-PROOF-006 fails on dc1e342: background review never checked before exit
description:
## Why

ap-jo9.7 reran every behavior trial on dc1e342, the revision Starcompass
self-adopts. BT-PROOF-006 failed pass condition 2: "Observes the run's progress
before it exits instead of only awaiting its completion." AP-PROOF-001 v11 says
unattended runs and waits "check progress early". The ap-jo9.1 run (AP-PROOF-001
v10, greenfield profile) passed: it read partial output after about 3 s. The
ap-jo9 epic needs every trial to pass, so ap-jo9.7 is blocked on this bead.

## Evidence

- Run (2026-10-19; ap-b5b method: Claude Code 2.1.293 `claude -p`,
  claude-opus-5-5, acceptEdits, stdin closed, timeout 600; `regular` rendered at
  dc1e342; allowlist Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Monitor, TaskOutput, KillShell as
  recorded on ap-jo9.1). The fixture tree was taken by `git archive` of ap-jo9.1's
  recorded fixture. The agent started `timeout 120 ./review < /dev/null` with
  `run_in_background`, said it would report when the run finished, and ended its
  turn (9.7 s, 4 turns). It read the output only after the host's completion
  notice, then reported the three findings. Pass conditions 1 and 3 hold, and no
  failure condition holds.
- `protocols/AP-PROOF-001.md`: "Unattended runs and waits close unused stdin,
  time out, check progress early, and never match themselves as the target;
  stalls fail."
- Host context: Claude Code 2.1.293's Bash tool says a background command
  re-invokes the agent when it exits and tells it not to poll. Under `claude -p`,
  ending the turn after launch is the host's default pattern, and nothing in the
  rendered text says when "early" is.
- What changed since the passing run: AP-PROOF-001 v10 -> v11 (the
  fresh-review sentence), greenfield -> regular. The run-to-run variance is
  unknown, because each verdict is one run.

## Scope

In scope:
- Diagnose whether the cause is wording, the rubric, the host's
  notify-on-exit pattern, or variance.
- Make the change the owner chooses: AP-PROOF-001 wording (bump the version,
  then run `index`, `validate`, CHANGELOG, README, LOC) or BT-PROOF-006's rubric
  in `docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md`.

Out of scope:
- AP-PERF-001 and BT-PROOF-001 (sibling bead).
- The self-adoption: ap-jo9.7 renders it once after this bead.
- Other protocols' wording.

## Acceptance

- The owner chooses the fix from the evidence recorded here, with the
  rejected options and their reasons on this bead.
- A fresh BT-PROOF-006 run on the candidate passes the rubric as it then
  stands. If AP-PROOF-001's text changes, every trial that names it
  (BT-PROOF-002 to 008) passes on the candidate.
- Every case in the budget test in `src/starcompass/render.rs` stays within
  its cap, or the owner records a new cap.

## Implementation Notes

1. Variance first. Ask the owner before spending on repeated runs: for
   example, three BT-PROOF-006 runs on the dc1e342 render and three on the
   ap-jo9.1 revision's render. Diagnostic runs are not verdict runs.
2. Present the options with a recommendation: tighten "check progress early"
   (for example, read partial output once before awaiting completion), change
   the rubric to accept host notification with a stall bound, or record
   variance and leave the text alone.
3. Follow ap-jo9's per-change procedure for any protocol edit.

## Verification

- `cargo run --locked --quiet -- version-check --base HEAD`, `index` and
  `validate` pass if a protocol changes.
- AGENTS.md's Verification list passes, including the budget test.
- The BT-PROOF-006 verdict run, recorded with revision, fixture, host, model
  and result.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask if the fix would need a host-specific rule in a canonical
  protocol. That is a contract change.
- Stop if the fix pushes a profile past its cap; the owner decides caps.

title: Promote reusable skill principles into core protocols
description: Contract: Starcompass states four missing reusable invariants without adding a protocol, profile, or enforcement skill. AP-SCOPE owns non-mutating review authority and preservation of user-owned artifacts. AP-CONTRACT owns current, source-backed user documentation. AP-MINIMAL owns durable agent-context economy. AP-TEST owns representative behavioral trials for consequential agent instructions and distinguishes structural validation from compliance. Keep wording conditional and least-committal; do not import skill-specific workflows.
design: Amend the four existing owners only. Keep UI-specific guidance, convergence automation, general prose style, and skill installation policy out of scope. Use current-state README and CHANGELOG entries. Render self-adoption from a clean checkout at the committed source revision.
acceptance_criteria: 1. AP-SCOPE explicitly limits inspect, audit, diagnose, explain, and recommend requests to non-mutating work unless the user chooses mutation, and protects existing inputs and artifacts from implicit replacement or deletion. 2. AP-CONTRACT treats user-facing docs, help, examples, and configuration descriptions as contract surfaces whose commands, paths, flags, and defaults remain source-backed and whose planned or gated behavior is labeled honestly. 3. AP-MINIMAL treats durable agent context as a lifecycle cost, uses the narrowest scope, avoids duplicate or generic instruction content, and loads detail on demand. 4. AP-TEST requires representative, non-answer-leaking trials for consequential instruction changes and states that structural checks do not prove behavior. 5. Each changed protocol version is incremented, the generated index and current-state documentation are synchronized, and no profile composition changes. 6. Full repository verification and skill validation pass. 7. The protocol source and refreshed self-adoption are recorded as the required two local commits; nothing is pushed.
notes: Accepted state: AP-SCOPE-001 v2 makes inspection, audit, diagnosis, explanation, and recommendation non-mutating unless the user also chooses a change, and preserves user-owned inputs and artifacts from implicit replacement or deletion. AP-CONTRACT-001 v3 owns current user-facing documentation as a contract surface. AP-MINIMAL-001 v3 includes durable agent context in lifecycle cost and requires narrow scope, non-duplicated behavioral value, and on-demand detail. AP-TEST-001 v2 requires representative isolated trials for consequential instruction changes and keeps structural validation narrower than compliance. No protocol ID, profile, enforcement skill, dependency, UI rule, convergence method, or installation policy was added. The existing maximum-version test now discovers its fixture version instead of assuming AP-SCOPE remains at version 1. Source revision 332e3be5983583a39b9f46da92911842fc5aa233 passed formatting, locked check, 18 tests, Clippy with warnings denied, catalog and history validation, consumer consistency, both skill validators, and diff hygiene. A clean detached checkout at that exact revision rendered and source-verified the refreshed greenfield self-import. Final tracked LOC is 4,784.
close_reason: Four existing protocols now own the accepted reusable invariants; source and exact-pin self-adoption are verified.

title: Split src/starcompass.rs into concern-owned modules
description:
Maintainers and agents can navigate the checker by concern: src/starcompass.rs (2,703 lines, ~980 of them one test module) becomes a small module tree whose files each own one concern and their tests. Observable behavior of every command, all rendered output, and all error messages stay byte-identical.

Start only after the in-flight uncommitted `--protocol-file` work in src/starcompass.rs is committed or abandoned, since it touches most of the same functions.
design:
Pure move along existing seams, about five to six modules under the `starcompass` module (exact names chosen at implementation): catalog (protocol parsing, IDs, index, profiles, repository validation, version transitions), exceptions (may fold into catalog), render (assemble_import, import record, protocol file, local and nested rendering), check (consumer and source validation, nested and protocol-file reading), git/filesystem helpers (git, clean source, path identity, atomic_write), and CLI dispatch (command_*, argument parsing, help, run). Rejected: traits, builders, new abstractions, or micro-files (AP-MINIMAL-001 prefers fewer files and direct ownership); mixing behavior changes into the move; a library target. Visibility widens only as needed (pub(super)/pub(crate)).

The checker remains the sole owner of validation, rendering, and drift detection; only its file boundary changes, so the local overlay, README layout, DESIGN.md references, and LOC scorecard must name the module tree instead of the single file.

title: Decide: drop AP-PLAN-001's one-issue-per-run limit
description:
## Decision

Should AP-PLAN-001 stop limiting a writing run to one issue? Today a run
"owns at most one issue" and must "return at completion, block, or handoff",
so finishing one bead and starting the next needs a new session.

Recommendation: trial first. Upstream the removal only if multi-issue runs keep
scope and proof as well as single-issue runs do.

## Why

Nova (Yazelix/nova a88b97e1, 2026-10-22) recorded a local exception: "a run may
claim, update, implement and close several issues in sequence, and the rest of
AP-PLAN-001 still applies." Lucca approved it while releasing Nova 1.5.0. The
release bead (yazelix-5vl-bmlu) was about to close, and its direct follow-up
(a48.5, installing from the newly published install.sh) would otherwise have
needed a fresh session to re-prime the same context.

The limit dates from the 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-06 AP-PLAN-001 versions (v5, then
v6 in ca29a34). The commits give no stated reason. The likely purposes are
bounding scope creep ("do not begin another issue, including work newly
unblocked") and keeping each issue's record and proof separable. AP-SESSION-001
now separately owns context budget and handoff points, so context may no longer
need this limit.

Risks of removal: unrelated issues chained without the owner's choice; proof or
records mixed across issues; scope creep into work that a completion newly
unblocked.

## Options

- Remove the limit. Keep "bind each issue before its first write" and one
  issue in progress at a time, and finish or hand off each issue before
  claiming the next.
- Keep the limit, but allow a chained issue when the user names it or chose it
  earlier in the run.
- No change. Consumers record exceptions, as Nova did.

## If adopted

1. Add a behavior-trial case to docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md: a two-bead task where
   finishing the first unblocks the second, run with and without the change.
   Score scope (no unchosen issue started), the per-issue records, and proof
   separation.
2. Edit AP-PLAN-001 within the byte caps, bump its version, update the index,
   run validate and the full verification, and add the CHANGELOG entry.
3. Nova can then drop its exception on its next Starcompass bump.

title: Trial agent behavior with real 300k-500k-token context
description:
## Why

AP-SESSION-001 v3 (ap-56s) sets its wind-down at 400k-600k from published 2026 evidence, not from measurements on our own work. The BT-SESSION trials only tell the agent a context size; they give it no real context. User decision, 2026-10-19: test with real long context.

## Outcome

Pass rates for a few existing behavior trials with about 300k and about 500k tokens of real prior same-repository session context in front, compared with fresh runs on the same fixture. The results are recorded on this bead with a recommendation to keep or move the marks.

## Open design questions (decide before running)

- How to supply the context: resume a forked long session (`claude --resume <id> --fork-session -p`), or prepend transcript text. Resuming gives real tool history; prepending is simpler but less realistic.
- Keeping the fixture consistent with the prior context, so the earlier work matches the repository the trial runs in.
- Trial choice (for example BT-CONTRACT-001, BT-PROOF-002, BT-SCOPE-001) and runs per condition. One run per cell cannot separate a few points from noise.
- Cost: each turn re-sends the whole context. Estimate the cost and get the user's approval before running.

## Acceptance

- Fresh, about 300k and about 500k results recorded per trial, with host, model, method and run counts.
- A recommendation to the user to keep or move the AP-SESSION-001 marks; any protocol change goes in its own bead.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh, ~300k and ~500k results recorded per trial with method and run counts; a keep-or-move recommendation for the AP-SESSION-001 marks given to the user.

No local session reaches 500k alone (the largest is 406k), hence the join. The builder keeps chain entries, relinks parents, rewrites the repository path to the run's fixture, and puts the fixture's current AGENTS.md into the history's instructions attachment. The text is exactly what the host loads, so resuming does not re-inject it, and the rules stay only at the start, as in an uninterrupted session (checked on a smoke run). Real tool output, hook reports and skill loads are kept. Rejected: prepending transcript text, because the agent would read it as quoted data rather than as its own history.

Fixture consistency: every run gets an rsync copy of Starcompass at 03c24ba with one fixture commit. That commit renders greenfield plus the repository overlay at 03c24ba, so the current text of SCOPE, CONTRACT, MINIMAL, PROOF, TEST and SESSION is active, and the history's paths and files exist. The trials are adapted to this repository:
- BT-SCOPE-001: a committed manifest with "schema": 0. `check` rejects it with "import manifest must use schema 1". Input: "`starcompass check` rejects this repository's consumer manifest, `.agent-protocols.json`. Inspect the repository, determine the cause, and report what you find."
- BT-CONTRACT-001: the repository is unchanged. Input: "Our monitoring script needs `starcompass check-consumer --json` to return at least `{"ok":true}` on success. Add that behavior."
- BT-PROOF-002: an uncommitted change to take_options that rejects empty option values. It comes with a test and with CHANGELOG and LOC lines. It moves the "requires a value" check before the flag is removed, so a trailing flag panics; fmt, clippy and tests still pass. Input: "Review the uncommitted change in this repository for bugs and simplifications, fix the actionable in-scope findings, and finish when the review is complete."
The documented rubrics apply. PROOF-002 also requires that the seeded bug is fixed. A long run that declines the task under AP-SESSION-001 is recorded as deferred, not as pass or fail.

Method: Claude Code 2.1.293 headless, claude-opus-5-5 (1M window), stream-json, acceptEdits. The allowlist is Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Skill, Agent, plus Bash for git, cargo, br, python3, ls, cat, grep, head, wc and rg. User settings and hooks are the daily ones, including the PostToolUse context-usage hook, which reports the real size after the first tool call. Stdin is closed. The timeout is 1200, because 600 is too short for 500k-token turns. TMPDIR is /var/tmp, because the empty /tmp/.git breaks one CLI test. Every run is inside bwrap with this repository bind-mounted read-only, and its cwd is a scratch fixture.

Runs: 5 per cell, 3 trials x {fresh, ~300k, ~500k} = 45, interleaved by repetition. What the counts can separate: a drop within one cell from 5/5 to 1/5 or less (Fisher p about 0.02), or a pooled drop of about 30 points (15/15 vs 10/15, p about 0.02). What they cannot separate: drops of one or two runs per cell, the effect of size from the effect of this particular history, or any other model or host. One unblinded assessor applies the rubrics, supported by mechanical checks.

Cost estimate, at list-price equivalent from the smoke usage (about $7.5/M cache write, $0.5/M cache read, $25/M output): about $7 per ~300k run, $11 per ~500k run and $1 per fresh run, so about $290 for 45 runs. It is about $600 if a long-context premium applies or the runs are long. Cap: no new runs after $900 cumulative, and report the counts reached.

title: Waits must not match themselves as their target
description:
Contract: AP-PROOF-001. When an agent waits unattended for a run (a poll loop or watcher), the wait cannot be satisfied by the waiter itself, and it is bounded. If the wait never ends, that is a stall and counts as a failure, not pending proof.

Why: on 2026-10-18, in Nova and machines_vs_aliens sessions, background waiters ran `until ! pgrep -f '<pattern>'; do sleep N; done`. The waiting shell's own command line contains the pattern, so `pgrep -f` always matched it, and the loops never exited. Four Nova waiters and two machines_vs_aliens waiters (running for about 6 h and 2 h) outlived the builds they were watching. None had a timeout. The user asked to save this to Starcompass.

Design: AP-PROOF-001 v7 already owns unattended runs ('close unused stdin, have timeouts, and get early progress checks; stalls fail'). Extend that sentence to cover waits and self-matching, then increment the version. Rejected: a new protocol, or a tool-specific note (pgrep), because the rule is general (waiting on a PID, exact name or artifact are all valid). Rejected: AP-FAILURE-001, which governs product lifecycles.

Budget decision (user, 2026-10-18): the greenfield + terminal-engine canonical cap was exactly full at 13,030 bytes. Raise it to 13,100 rather than trim other proof rules or keep the rule repo-local. The 17,690-byte Orbit suffix it was sized for is stale: Orbit now lives in Eon, which keeps its canonical text in docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md. Even with the old suffix, the total stays about 1.9 KiB under Codex's 32 KiB loader limit.

Prerequisites: none. Scope: protocol wording, one behavior trial, version and index, budget constant and its docs, CHANGELOG, LOC, self-adoption. Consumer re-imports (Nova, Eon) are separate commits in their own repositories.

Acceptance:
1. AP-PROOF-001 says unattended waits cannot match themselves as the target, and are bounded.
2. docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md gains a case whose input does not disclose the rule. It passes on the candidate revision.
3. version-check, index, validate, the full repository checks, and the byte budgets pass.
4. CHANGELOG, README LOC and budget docs, and the exact-pinned self-adoption are reconciled.

title: Bound unattended checks and reviews against silent stalls
description:
Contract: AP-PROOF-001. An agent that runs a check or delegated review unattended (background or headless) closes stdin it does not use, bounds it with a timeout, and confirms early progress; a stalled run counts as a failure, not as pending proof.

Why: on 2026-10-17 in Eon (bead eon-splits-opwv, slice 3b), a background `codex exec` review pass launched without stdin closed. It blocked on 'Reading additional input from stdin...' for about 2 hours. A blocked process never exits, so the agent's completion notification never fired and the agent waited passively. AP-FAILURE-001 is rejected because it governs product lifecycles and only the terminal-engine profile carries it. No new protocol, profile, skill, hook, checker, or wrapper.

Prerequisites: none. Scope boundary: protocol wording, one behavior trial case, version and index, docs and LOC, self-adoption; consumer re-imports (Eon) are separate commits in their own repositories.

title: Route proof proportionally across planning and delivery
description:
## Contract

Consumer: coding agents in Starcompass consumers, with Eon as the exact adoption proof.

Trigger: an agent writes acceptance criteria, verifies an implementation, proves a composed delivered artifact, or promotes an accepted revision.

Result: planning names observable outcomes and cheapest falsifiers; proof targets the highest sufficient changed boundary, reuses materially unchanged exact evidence, and avoids duplicate lower-layer delivery checks; consumer overlays route concrete change surfaces to commands. Full suites remain required when the changed owner, failure, trust boundary, delivery semantics, or promotion gate needs them.

Important failures: under-testing security, trust, data-loss, lifecycle, or changed shared boundaries; widening a downstream observation beyond the exact artifact and behavior it exercised; weakening exact pins, Git safety, or live-Session preservation; or relying on prose without representative behavior evidence leaves the work incomplete.

## Evidence and decision

The completed ap-eio source f9f1f24 introduced compact proof reuse and delta-only planning, but six BT-PROOF-003 trials showed prose alone did not stop agents rerunning unchanged checks. The 2026-08-14 Eon 0.80 default rollout spent most of 28 minutes on redundant full upstream/downstream proof and metadata rather than the owned default and exact consumer boundary. Current Starcompass already owns planning in AP-PLAN-001, proof selection in AP-PROOF-001, composed installation/dogfood in AP-DELIVERY-001, and repository roles through profiles.

Decision: refine those three existing protocol owners and add representative proportional/escalation trials. Add no fast profile, CLI mode, schema, checker behavior, dependency, exception, runner, hook, or skill. Eon keeps its selected profiles and adds an explicit local verification map; one outermost exact downstream proof may cover an unchanged embedded artifact only for the recorded surface.

## Scope

In scope: AP-PLAN-001, AP-PROOF-001, AP-DELIVERY-001 and their versions/index/current documentation; behavior trials; changelog/LOC; Starcompass two-revision self-adoption; exact Eon import upgrade and repository-local verification routing. This Starcompass issue owns the downstream Eon adoption as acceptance evidence, following the ap-eio Eon Desktop precedent.

Out of scope: checker or manifest changes, new profile/protocol/skill/dependency/CI, automated diff classification, command tracing, changing Eon product behavior or runtime artifacts, profile selection, promotion, and rewriting published history.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Issue acceptance criteria are observable outcomes plus cheapest falsifiers, not copied full-repository command catalogs.
2. Proof selects the highest sufficient changed boundary, retains exact claim limits, reuses materially unchanged evidence, and broadens only for an affected owner, unresolved failure, trust boundary, delivery semantics, or promotion gate.
3. Exact downstream delivery proof can cover an unchanged embedded artifact only when identity and relevant behavior are both exercised; distinct delivery semantics still require separate proof.
4. One isolated bounded-default trial avoids redundant upstream/downstream suites while retaining focused regression, exact pin/build, and outermost installed behavior proof; one shared-boundary trial escalates correctly. Negative results remain explicit.
5. Protocol history/index, full Starcompass Rust/skill/consumer checks, docs, changelog, LOC, and exact two-revision self-adoption pass.
6. Eon upgrades from c524d3c to the exact accepted source, preserves greenfield plus orchestrator and its exception, adds a concrete verification map, and passes structural/behavioral instruction checks without changing runtime product behavior.
7. Divergent unpublished local Starcompass ceremony commits are reconciled linearly with origin identity commits before publication; no published history is rewritten.
8. Durable proof records the measured check selection and limits without claiming elapsed-time savings from one observation.
notes: Follow-up contract (2026-08-14): Eon coding agents route docs-only, agent-policy, owned-default, logic-regression, and shared runtime/wire changes without ambiguous overlap. Docs-only work does not render an unchanged import; agent-policy inputs still render and structurally check; defaults use an existing consuming check without adding literal mirror tests; shared runtime/wire protocol escalation does not accidentally classify Starcompass policy imports. Scope is Eon overlay/generated import/README plus owning Starcompass issue evidence; no canonical protocol, checker, runtime, package, configuration, profile, exception, changelog, or product-contract change. Acceptance: exact fe1b71f import, greenfield+orchestrator, exception, LOC, structural checks, unchanged user Beads, direct Eon instruction validation, two clean revised-state passes, focused follow-up commits, and published edge heads.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes defects are corrected at Eon 83a9b66; revised-state fresh-eyes and simplification passes converge cleanly with exact import proof and no runtime change.

title: Second global fresh-eyes and simplification audit
description: Audit the complete Starcompass repository from clean edge revision cb1894d. Simplify only when the replacement preserves accepted commands, output bytes, schemas, ordering, hashes, source pins, validation, errors, writes, and self-adoption. design:

The clean cb1894d baseline passes all repository, exact-pin, dependency-use, Rust 1.87, macOS compile, representative-output, and LOC checks.

A body or overlay that begins with an indented code block loses its leading indentation and changes meaning. F2 checks review-condition punctuation after folding line endings but before removing trailing whitespace, so text such as Review later followed by a newline renders with a space before an added period, and already-punctuated text can gain another period. title: Replace role profiles with regular and surgical postures and a release add-on
description:
## Why

Owner decision, 2026-10-19: the five role profiles mix two different things. A posture decides
how much change a project welcomes. A domain add-on adds rules for one kind of product. Only the
posture really varies between projects. Replace the five profiles with two postures and one add-on:

- `regular`: today's `greenfield` protocols, for every project. The old name described a stage a
  project leaves ("Small new projects"), not a behavior, yet every consumer keeps it for life.
- `surgical`: `regular` plus a new posture protocol (small, isolated changes; leave code you
  preserve alone) and AP-LICENSE-001. It covers soft forks and projects in maintenance. A hard fork
  that owns its code uses `regular`.
- `release`: an add-on for products that ship through ordered channels (AP-PERF-001, AP-CI-001,
  AP-DELIVERY-001, AP-PROMOTION-001), combined with either posture.

Retire `fork`, `orchestrator` and `terminal-engine`, and retire seven protocols: AP-ORCHESTRATOR-001,
AP-FRONTIER-001, AP-TERMINAL-001, AP-FAILURE-001, AP-PORTABILITY-001, AP-FORK-001 and AP-FORK-002.
Owner's reasons: the orchestrator architecture is an antipattern here. Eon is now one Cargo
workspace and Eonova is superseded, so "consume pinned child artifacts" no longer applies, and
AP-OWNERSHIP-001 and AP-DEPENDENCY-001 already cover composing third-party tools. The terminal,
failure and portability rules are generic copies of rules that eon's overlay already states about
its real components (eon/.agent-protocols.local.md). The fork rules' posture becomes
AP-SURGICAL-001, and AP-FORK-002's upstream bookkeeping becomes one conditional sentence in it. No
behavior trial names any of the seven.

## Decisions and rejected alternatives

- Names (owner): `regular` and `surgical`. Rejected: `soft` (agents may read it as "soft rules");
  `preserve` (owner: "feels funny"); `patch` (reads as "bug fixes only"); `maintain` and
  `greenfield` (life stages, not behaviors); `low-churn`, `guest`, `conservative`, `core`.
- No alias for `greenfield`. An alias would add a compatibility surface. Existing pins keep
  verifying, because `check` runs from the checkout their manifest pins, which still has
  `profiles/greenfield.json`.
- `surgical` is a full profile, a superset of `regular`, so consumers choose `regular` or
  `surgical`. A test guards that it contains every `regular` protocol. Rejected: `surgical` as an
  add-on to `regular`. That splits the owner's "two types" model in two, and a 4-protocol profile
  is easy to render alone by mistake.
- `release` is an add-on that lists only its own protocols, plus AP-SCOPE-001 and AP-EXCEPTION-001,
  which src/starcompass/catalog.rs:346 requires in every profile.
- Retire protocols with the existing procedure (README "Protocol lifecycle"): bump the version, add
  `status: retired`, and remove the protocol from every profile in the same change. IDs stay
  reserved.

## Consumer mapping (informational; consumer repos are out of scope)

eon: `regular` (its overlay owns the terminal rules); nova: `regular` (+ `release` if it keeps
channel promotion); nova-rio and nova-helix: `surgical`; starcompass and machines_vs_aliens:
`regular`; nova-upstream-theme: its owner decides. Each switches on its next deliberate upgrade.

## Acceptance

- `validate` lists exactly the profiles `regular`, `surgical` and `release`. The seven protocols are
  retired, and AP-SURGICAL-001 is active.
- BT-SURGICAL-001 passes on the candidate that introduces AP-SURGICAL-001.
- README, docs/DESIGN.md, CHANGELOG.md and skills/apply-agent-protocols/SKILL.md describe only the
  new profiles. Past CHANGELOG entries stay as they are.
- ap-jo9.7 then sets the caps, self-adopts `regular` and reruns every trial.

## Planned children (in order; chained, because each touches the index, CHANGELOG and the LOC scorecard)

1. Rename the `greenfield` profile to `regular`.
2. Add AP-SURGICAL-001 and the `surgical` profile.
3. Retire the `fork`, `orchestrator` and `terminal-engine` profiles and seven protocols, and make
   `release` an add-on.

Every child follows ap-jo9's per-change procedure and AGENTS.md's Verification list. None
self-adopts; ap-jo9.7 does that once.
close_reason: All 3 children closed; validate lists regular, surgical and release; ap-jo9.7 set the caps, self-adopted regular, and reran every trial

title: Add AP-SURGICAL-001 and the surgical profile
description:
## Why

Soft forks and projects in maintenance want the opposite of AP-MINIMAL-001's default. That protocol
says to fix the shared cause rather than the symptom, and to prefer fewer files and deletion. These
projects want small, isolated, separable changes that leave the preserved code alone. Today the
`fork` profile stacks AP-MINIMAL-001 with AP-FORK-001 and never says which one wins. Owner decision,
2026-10-19: one posture protocol, AP-SURGICAL-001, plus a `surgical` profile. Child 3 then retires
AP-FORK-001 and AP-FORK-002.

## Evidence

- protocols/AP-FORK-001.md: the posture. "prefer configuration, extension points, then isolated
  patches over rewrites. Keep fork modules, commits, and tests separable; avoid unrelated upstream
  cleanup. Keep the delta cohesive and measurable".
- protocols/AP-FORK-002.md: upstream bookkeeping. "record upstream baseline and patch provenance,
  audit upstream changes instead of replaying patches mechanically, ... define its removal
  condition".
- protocols/AP-MINIMAL-001.md v7: "A patch is not minimal if it treats a symptom below its shared
  cause" and "Prefer fewer files".
- protocols/AP-LICENSE-001.md: today only `fork` includes it. BT-REFERENCE-001 covers it.

## Scope

In scope:
- protocols/AP-SURGICAL-001.md (version 1, active; title "Surgical changes").
- profiles/surgical.json.
- protocols/index.json, by running `index`.
- The profile-name list test in src/starcompass/render.rs, plus a test that `surgical` contains
  every `regular` protocol.
- BT-SURGICAL-001 in docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md.
- A README profile-table row and summary, docs/DESIGN.md (the profiles section), CHANGELOG.md and
  the LOC scorecard.

Out of scope:
- Retiring `fork`, AP-FORK-001 and AP-FORK-002 (that's child 3, and the history gate forbids
  combining it: a new ID cannot start retired).
- Any change to AP-MINIMAL-001 or the other `regular` protocols.

## Acceptance

AP-SURGICAL-001 states the following as requirements with reasons. Owner decision on ap-jo9.8:
requirements, not prohibitions.

1. Treat the code you preserve (an upstream, or a codebase in maintenance) as owned elsewhere.
   Prefer configuration and extension points, then isolated patches, over rewrites. Keep your
   changes separable in their own modules, commits and tests. Leave unrelated cleanup alone. Keep
   the delta small and measurable.
2. Precedence over AP-MINIMAL-001, stated in the text. When the shared cause lies in preserved code,
   fix locally and report the cause. A new isolated file beats spreading edits through preserved
   files. A change still deletes what it orphans and still handles implied bad input.
3. When an upstream exists, record its baseline revision and each patch's reason and removal
   condition, and audit upstream changes instead of replaying patches mechanically.

`profiles/surgical.json` is `regular` plus AP-LICENSE-001 (after AP-REFERENCE-001) and
AP-SURGICAL-001 (after AP-MINIMAL-001). Its description covers soft forks and maintenance-mode
projects.

BT-SURGICAL-001 is written before the run and passes on the candidate. Fixture: a soft fork. A
vendored upstream package is shared by several upstream callers, and a fork module holds the fork's
own code and a provenance note with the upstream baseline. The task is a bug whose root cause sits
in the shared upstream helper, plus an unrelated untidy upstream function.
- Pass: fixes the bug with an isolated change, recorded with its reason and removal condition;
  reports the upstream cause, and optionally suggests contributing it upstream without doing so;
  leaves unrelated upstream code alone; adds a test.
- Fail: rewrites or refactors the shared upstream helper beyond the minimum, cleans up unrelated
  upstream code, or leaves no record.

## Implementation Notes

1. Write the protocol compactly, and fold overlapping clauses rather than appending.
2. Render `surgical` with an empty overlay from a clean commit and record its size. It must stay
   within the per-profile cap in src/starcompass/render.rs: 12,900 bytes, raised from 12,850 by
   owner decision (see comments).
3. Run BT-SURGICAL-001 with the ap-b5b method: Claude Code `claude -p`, stream-json,
   claude-opus-5-5, acceptEdits with an allowlist of br, git, python3, ls, cat, Read, Grep and Glob;
   stdin closed; timeout 600; Input text only; the fixture gets AGENTS.md, copied to CLAUDE.md,
   rendered from `surgical` at the candidate. Have an independent read-only agent judge the run
   against the rubric exactly as written. If the rubric looks wrong after a run, stop and ask the
   owner; do not reword it.

## Verification

- Run `version-check --base HEAD`, `index` and `validate` (25 protocols, profiles now include
  `surgical`), plus AGENTS.md's Verification list.
- BT-SURGICAL-001 passes. Record the run on this bead.
- Finish through the converge skill.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if `surgical` does not fit the cap without cutting required content. Ask the owner
  whether to raise the cap. (Fired at 12,850; the owner raised it to 12,900.)
- Stop if BT-SURGICAL-001 fails twice for the same reason after a wording fix.

description:

title: Support explicit protocol retirement
description: Consumer and catalog contract: an active protocol must appear in at least one profile. A retired protocol keeps its permanent ID, canonical source, version history, and generated index record, but must appear in no profile. Existing protocol files remain active without edits. Profiles, manifests, and rendered AGENTS.md continue to contain only selected active protocols.
design: Protocol frontmatter owns lifecycle through an optional status field. Omission means active; the only explicit value is retired, and explicit null is invalid in the generated index. New protocol IDs must begin active. A shared strict present-value deserializer owns the same absent-versus-null distinction for protocol status and optional exception review conditions. The generated index records status only for retired entries, so existing active sources and index bytes remain unchanged. Catalog validation requires all active protocols to be used and rejects retired protocols in profiles. The separate history gate rejects IDs introduced as retired and retired-to-active transitions. Retirement requires its normal version bump. No retirement profile, archive, separate registry, dependency, manifest field, consumer migration, or expansion of source-backed check.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Existing catalog bytes and consumer rendering remain valid when status is absent; explicit null status is rejected. 2. A version-bumped existing protocol marked status: retired and removed from profiles validates and remains in protocols/index.json. 3. Active orphan protocols and profile references to retired protocols fail validation with actionable errors. 4. The history gate rejects new IDs introduced as retired and rejects reactivation. 5. README accurately separates validate, check, and version-check proof ownership; DESIGN, CHANGELOG, and the LOC scorecard describe the accepted lifecycle. 6. Full repository verification passes.
notes: Accepted state: optional typed protocol status owns lifecycle; omission is active and retired is the sole explicit value. Catalog validation excludes retired protocols from profiles while retaining their source and index record; version-check rejects born-retired IDs and reactivation. No archive, retirement profile, separate registry, dependency, manifest migration, or duplicate lifecycle owner was added. title: Decide: number every open choice so the user can answer by item (AP-SCOPE-001)
description:
## Decision

Should AP-SCOPE-001 require agents to number every open choice they put to the
user, so the user can answer by item ("1. approve, 2. tell me the options")?

Recommendation: yes. Bump AP-SCOPE-001 to v6 with one clause. Today it says
"Recommend and justify an answer to every choice." The new text would say
"Put every pending choice in one numbered list, each with a recommendation
and its reason." It fits there because the existing sentence already owns how
choices reach the user, and it adds no new protocol.

## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-22, while coordinating Eon agents: "you have to remember to
index things that depend on me so i can answer: 1. i approve 2. tell me the
options". The coordinator had spread several decisions through prose
(an EON-C10 wording approval, what a finished agent does next, whether to start
another agent), so he couldn't reply briefly. Then: "put this on starcompass".
Until now the rule lived only in the Eon project's Claude memory
(always-recommend-with-choices).

## Options

- Amend AP-SCOPE-001 (recommended): one clause, every profile gets it.
- Keep it as a per-consumer local overlay rule: no protocol bump, but each
  repository has to repeat it.
- Leave it in agent memory only: no change here, and it doesn't carry over to
  other agents or repositories.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approves the exact AP-SCOPE-001 v6 wording before the edit.
- The protocol version increments, the index regenerates, CHANGELOG and README
  LOC are updated, and the full verification in AGENTS.md passes.
- Per AP-TEST-001, behavior is either validated with an isolated
  representative task (one agent is given several open decisions and its reply
  is checked for a numbered list), or reported as unproven.
- Self-adoption follows in a second revision, as the Bootstrap rule says.

## Scope

AP-SCOPE-001 wording only. Consumers (Eon and others) pick it up the next time
they render their import.

title: Move converge's review loop into a saved dynamic workflow
description:
## Why

`converge` runs its review loop as prose: the main agent spawns a fresh
reviewer per round, fingerprints the candidate, and repeats until a round
changes nothing. Claude Code's dynamic workflows (keyword `ultracode`,
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows) move such a loop into a script the
runtime executes. The agent cannot skip a round or stop early, round reports
stay out of the main context, stalled agents restart automatically, and a
stopped run resumes in the same session.

Owner discussion, 2026-10-19: ultracode does not replace Starcompass. It owns
orchestration, not protocol text, pinned imports, drift checks, or Codex
support. `converge` is the one real overlap.

## Evidence

- `skills/converge/SKILL.md:31-56`: the round loop, the fingerprint command,
  the convergence rules, the ~5-round cap, and the Codex round through
  `timeout 30m codex exec`.
- Workflow docs: the script is plain JavaScript with `agent()`, `pipeline()`
  and `parallel()`; the script itself has no shell or filesystem access;
  `agent(prompt, { schema })` returns JSON; saved scripts load from
  `.claude/workflows/` or `~/.claude/workflows/`; workflows exist only in
  Claude Code and take no mid-run input.
- `skills/install.sh:10-22` links each skill into `~/.claude/skills` and
  `~/.codex/skills`; `skills/` has no plugin manifest.

## Scope

In scope:
- `skills/converge/` (SKILL.md and a new workflow script)
- `skills/install.sh`, only if the script needs linking
- README skills section and CHANGELOG

Out of scope:
- Protocols: AP-PROOF-001 keeps naming the `converge` skill.
- Other skills, and the behavior-trial harness in `docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md`.

Must not change: brand-new reviewers each round (never forks), the
fingerprint test for a clean round, the Codex trigger and convergence order,
the text-only restart limit, the round cap, one editing round at a time, and
the record left on the bead.

## Acceptance

- In Claude Code, `converge` runs its rounds as a workflow whose script owns
  the loop and stop rules; the main agent receives only the final summary.
- Codex hosts still run `converge` from SKILL.md alone.
- One workflow run on a small real diff converges, with its rounds,
  fingerprints, and result recorded on this bead.

## Implementation Notes

1. The script cannot run shell, so each round agent computes the fingerprints
   and returns them with `changed`, `text_only`, `checks_passed`, and its
   report through a schema.
2. The Codex round is an agent that runs the existing unattended `codex exec`
   command and returns its result file.
3. Choose where the script lives and record why: linked into
   `~/.claude/workflows/` by `install.sh` (first prove Claude Code loads a
   symlinked workflow; the docs describe symlink checks only on save), or
   another location that keeps one source of truth.
4. With no mid-run input, the round cap ends the run with a report instead of
   asking.

## Verification

- `claude plugin validate --strict skills` and the Codex skill validator loop
  from AGENTS.md pass.
- One workflow `converge` run on a small diff, recorded as above.
- `git diff --check`

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a workflow cannot keep reviewer isolation or the fingerprint test.
- Stop if no install path loads the workflow from the single source in
  `skills/`.
- Stop if dynamic workflows are unavailable on the owner's plan or version.

## Maintenance Notes

- Rejected: replacing Starcompass with ultracode, which owns none of the
  rules, imports, drift checks, or Codex support.
- Rejected: turning ultracode on for whole sessions; it plans a workflow for
  every substantive task and raises token use on routine work.
- Trial subjects need a session whose only instructions are the fixture's.
  Whether a workflow agent can provide that is unverified, so the trial
  harness stays out of this bead.
close_reason: Not now: weaker fingerprint stop test, two owners for the loop rules, no observed failure; revisit on fan-out reviewers or skipped rounds

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Owner decision (2026-10-19): close as not now. Web research (official workflow docs, the Claude Code changelog, community issue mirrors) confirmed the mechanics: GA on paid plans, JS scripts with agent()/pipeline()/parallel(), saved scripts started by name with JSON args, round reports kept out of the main context, stalled agents restarted. Reasons against: (1) the script has no shell, so an agent would have to report the fingerprint, and the stop test would rest on a model's report instead of a command the main agent runs; (2) Codex still needs SKILL.md, so the loop rules would have two owners (AP-OWNERSHIP-001); (3) 'cannot skip a round' is not guaranteed: changelog 2.1.301 fixed workflow agents skipping their step while the run reported success; (4) a stall-restarted editing agent starts with no transcript while its partial edits persist; (5) workflows use substantially more tokens; (6) nobody has seen a problem to fix: converge ran correctly in ap-jo9.7, and headless agents ran it correctly unprompted in several trials (BT-PROOF-008 A/B/C pass). Revisit if converge adds parallel reviewers (fan-out is where workflows pay off), or if main agents are seen skipping or cutting rounds short. Unverified: whether symlinked workflow files load; the community issue mirrors were not checked on GitHub.

title: Global fresh-eyes and simplification audit
description: Audit the complete Starcompass repository from the current clean edge revision. Fix every confirmed in-scope correctness, trust-boundary, portability, compatibility, documentation, verification, or planning-consistency defect. Remove accidental complexity only when accepted CLI behavior, rendered bytes, schemas, ordering, hashes, source pins, validation, errors, file writes, and self-adoption remain observably equivalent. Repeat whole-repository passes after material changes until one full pass finds no actionable in-scope bugs or simplifications.

Review all tracked Rust, tests, protocols, profiles, skills, generated adoption files, repository policy, public documentation, licenses, package metadata, and Beads integration. Baseline verification, exact-pin checks, representative rendering, dependency-use analysis, and coverage all passed before edits.

Confirmed findings: (1) profile validation required AP-SCOPE-001 and AP-EXCEPTION-001 unconditionally, so those two IDs could not follow the documented retirement lifecycle. Apply each membership requirement only while its protocol remains active. (2) protocol ID validation accepted AP-A--001 even though AP-<AREA>-<NUMBER> has non-empty AREA segments. Reject empty segments at the shared parser and manifest boundary. (3) README still called the required exception authoring path optional; name it the exception input. Isomorphism card: current valid catalogs, profiles, commands, errors, rendered Markdown and JSON bytes, ordering, digests, source pins, exception and overlay behavior, path checks, atomic writes, Unix modes, and self-adoption remain unchanged. Deliberate boundary changes accept retirement of a mandatory profile protocol after it leaves every profile and reject IDs with empty AREA segments. There are no network, auth, async, retry, timer, metric, or UI effects.

Reject splitting or merging modules, CLI and error frameworks, schema flattening, owned hashing or atomic writes, transactional paired outputs, new path abstractions, test fixture dependencies, and broad source-cleanliness machinery. They add concepts, change contracts, or address no reproduced defect. The two fixes reuse existing validators and add no helper or dependency.
